Let $M$ be a Kripke model, and identify each fixpoint-free formula with
its embedding into the μ-calculus. For a μ-calculus formula $\psi$, a world $w$ and a stack $s$
of fixpoint binders, the Wins-guided move at the game position $(\psi, w, s)$ is the following
position. If $s$ is empty and $\psi$ is a fixpoint-free disjunction $\psi_1 \lor \psi_2$, it is
$(\psi_1, w, [])$ when $\psi_1$ is winning at $w$ (in the backward-induction winning region of
the fixpoint-free fragment) and $(\psi_2, w, [])$ otherwise. If $s$ is empty and $\psi$ is a
fixpoint-free formula $\Diamond \psi_1$, it is $(\psi_1, v, [])$ for a chosen successor $v$ of
$w$ at which $\psi_1$ is winning, if one exists; otherwise $(\psi_1, v, [])$ for a chosen
successor $v$ of $w$, if one exists; otherwise $(\psi, w, [])$. In every other case: at a
disjunction $\varphi_1 \lor \varphi_2$ it is $(\varphi_1, w, s)$; at $\Diamond \varphi_1$ it is
$(\varphi_1, v, s)$ for a chosen successor $v$ of $w$ if one exists, and $(\psi, w, s)$
otherwise; at $\nu \varphi_1$ it is $(\varphi_1, w, s')$, where $s'$ is $s$ with
$\nu \varphi_1$ pushed on top; and at every remaining formula (the positions owned by Refuter)
it is $(\psi, w, s)$.

Only the left disjunct is tested: if a fixpoint-free disjunction is winning at $w$ and its left
disjunct is not, then its right disjunct is.

## Sources

- C. Stirling, *Modal and Temporal Properties of Processes*, Springer 2001, Chapter 6.

articles.title: Wins-guided strategy wins finite plays (auxiliary induction)
articles.statement:
The Wins-guided strategy wins every complete finite play from a winning
fragment position.

articles.title: Wins-guided strategy wins every complete finite play
articles.statement:
The Wins-guided strategy wins every complete finite play from a winning
fragment position.

articles.title: Wins-guided strategy
articles.statement:
For a Kripke model $M$, the Wins-guided strategy is the Verifier
strategy of the model-checking game on $M$ that chooses, at each game position $(\psi, w, s)$,
the Wins-guided move at $(\psi, w, s)$. At every Verifier-owned position that has a move, this
choice is a legal move.

articles.title: Backward-induction winning region of the fixpoint-free fragment
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a Kripke
model with accessibility relation $R$. For a fixpoint-free formula $\varphi$ and a world $w$,
"$\varphi$ is winning at $w$" is defined by recursion on $\varphi$: an atom $a$ is winning at
$w$ iff $a$ is true at $w$ in $M$; a negated atom $\lnot a$ iff $a$ is not true at $w$; $\bot$
is never winning and $\top$ is always winning; $\varphi \land \psi$ is winning at $w$ iff both
$\varphi$ and $\psi$ are; $\varphi \lor \psi$ iff $\varphi$ or $\psi$ is; $\Box \varphi$ iff
$\varphi$ is winning at every $v$ with $w \mathrel{R} v$; and $\Diamond \varphi$ iff $\varphi$
is winning at some $v$ with $w \mathrel{R} v$.

Verifier has a winning strategy in the model-checking game from the position $(\varphi, w, [])$
with empty stack exactly when $\varphi$ is winning at $w$.

articles.title: Sequences that stay at the win state are won by the even player
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a Kripke
model and $\mathit{env}$ an environment for free variables. If an infinite sequence
$\pi_0 \pi_1 \pi_2 \dots$ of positions of the totalized fragment game of $M$ and $\mathit{env}$
has a $k_0$ such that $\pi_n$ is the absorbing winning state for all $n \ge k_0$, then $\pi$ is
won by the even player in that game.

articles.title: Sequences that stay at the lose state are won by the odd player
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a Kripke
model and $\mathit{env}$ an environment for free variables. If an infinite sequence
$\pi_0 \pi_1 \pi_2 \dots$ of positions of the totalized fragment game of $M$ and $\mathit{env}$
has a $k_0$ such that $\pi_n$ is the absorbing losing state for all $n \ge k_0$, then $\pi$ is
won by the odd player in that game.

articles.title: Contradiction yields falsity
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let
$\varphi$ be a modal formula. If both $\varphi$ and its negation $\neg\varphi$ are local
consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then
so is $\bot$.

articles.title: The monotonicity rule for necessity
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and let
$\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. If $\varphi \to \psi$ is a theorem of the normal modal logic
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then so is $\Box\varphi \to \Box\psi$.

articles.title: Consequences of no hypotheses are the theorems
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas.
A modal formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the empty set of hypotheses in the normal modal
logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ if and only if $\varphi$ is a theorem of
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: The deduction theorem for local modal consequence
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of
modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. In the normal modal logic
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\psi\}$ if and only
if $\psi \to \varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$.

articles.title: Local consequence in a normal modal logic
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal
formulas. The local consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ form the least set of modal formulas that contains every member of
$\Gamma$ and every theorem of $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ and is closed under modus ponens: whenever
it contains $\varphi \to \psi$ and $\varphi$, it contains $\psi$.

Necessitation applies to theorems only, not to hypotheses.

articles.title: Theorems of a normal modal logic
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas. The theorems of
the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ form the least set of modal formulas that
contains, for all modal formulas $\varphi$, $\psi$, $\chi$, the propositional axioms
$\varphi \to (\psi \to \varphi)$,
$(\varphi \to (\psi \to \chi)) \to ((\varphi \to \psi) \to (\varphi \to \chi))$ and
$\neg\neg\varphi \to \varphi$ (where $\neg\varphi$ is $\varphi \to \bot$) and the distribution
axiom $\Box(\varphi \to \psi) \to (\Box\varphi \to \Box\psi)$, that contains every member of
$\Lambda$, and that is closed under modus ponens (from $\varphi \to \psi$ and $\varphi$ infer
$\psi$) and necessitation (from $\varphi$ infer $\Box\varphi$).

articles.title: Compactness of local modal consequence
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal
formulas. If a modal formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the
normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then there is a finite set
$\Delta \subseteq \Gamma$ such that $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Delta$ in
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: The deduction theorem for local modal consequence, forward direction
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and
$\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. If $\varphi$ is a
local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\psi\}$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$,
then $\psi \to \varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Self-implication is a theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas. For every modal
formula $\varphi$, the formula $\varphi \to \varphi$ is a theorem of the normal modal logic
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Hypothetical syllogism
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let
$\varphi$, $\psi$, $\chi$ be modal formulas. If $\varphi \to \psi$ and $\psi \to \chi$ are local
consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then
so is $\varphi \to \chi$.

articles.title: Extra axioms of the modal logic K
articles.statement:
The set of extra axioms of the normal modal logic K is
the empty set of modal formulas over a given type of atoms; that is, K adds no axioms to the
propositional axioms and the distribution axiom.

articles.title: Monotonicity of local consequence in the hypotheses
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$, $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$
be sets of modal formulas with $\Gamma \subseteq \Delta$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local
consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then
$\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Delta$ in $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of theorems in the extra axioms
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'$ be sets of
modal formulas. Every theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ is a theorem of
$\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda'$.

articles.title: Double-negation introduction
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas. If a
formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic
$\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then so is $\neg\neg\varphi$, where $\neg\psi$ abbreviates
$\psi \to \bot$.

articles.title: Negation introduction
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and $\varphi$ a
formula. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma \cup \{\varphi\}$ in the normal
modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\neg\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in
$\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, where $\neg\varphi$ abbreviates $\varphi \to \bot$.

articles.title: Consistency of K
articles.statement:
For every type of atoms, $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal
logic K, the logic with no extra axioms.

articles.title: Consistency of S4
articles.statement:
For every type of atoms, $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal
logic S4, whose extra axioms are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ and
$\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$.

articles.title: Consistency of S5
articles.statement:
For every type of atoms, $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal
logic S5, whose extra axioms are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ and
$\Diamond\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates
$\neg\Box\neg\varphi$ and $\neg\psi$ abbreviates $\psi \to \bot$.

articles.title: Consistency of T
articles.statement:
For every type of atoms, $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal
logic T, whose extra axioms are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$.

articles.title: Consistency of normal modal logics
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas each of which
is valid in the one-world Kripke model whose world sees itself and in which every atom is false.
Then $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Ex falso quodlibet
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $\Gamma$ a set of
hypotheses. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then every formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Local consequences of theorems are theorems
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas
and let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas each of which is a theorem of the normal modal logic
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in
$\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a theorem of $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Proof by contradiction
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $\Gamma$ a set of
hypotheses and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of
$\Gamma \cup \{\neg\varphi\}$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then
$\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Extra axioms of S4
articles.statement:
The extra axioms of the modal logic S4 are the formulas
$\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T) and $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$ (axiom 4), for all
modal formulas $\varphi$.

articles.title: Extra axioms of S5
articles.statement:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, write $\Diamond\varphi$ for
$\neg\Box\neg\varphi$. The extra axioms of the modal logic S5 are the formulas
$\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T) and $\Diamond\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$ (axiom 5), for
all modal formulas $\varphi$.

articles.title: Local soundness
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\Lambda$ a set of modal formulas each
of which is valid in $M$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of a set $\Gamma$ of
formulas in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ holds at every
world of $M$ at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Extra axioms of T
articles.statement:
The extra axioms of the modal logic T are the formulas
$\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T), for all modal formulas $\varphi$.

articles.title: Transitivity of local consequence
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and let
$\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be sets of formulas such that every formula of $\Delta$ is a local
consequence of $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$. If a formula
$\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Delta$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a
local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: The one-world model has an equivalence relation
articles.statement:
The accessibility relation of the
one-world Kripke model, whose single world sees itself and at which every atom is false, is an
equivalence relation.

articles.title: The one-world Kripke model
articles.statement:
For any type of atoms, the one-world Kripke model has a
single world, which sees itself, and every atom is false at that world.

articles.title: Soundness of K for Kripke models
articles.statement:
Every theorem of the modal logic K is valid in every
Kripke model: if a formula $\varphi$ is derivable in K, then $\varphi$ holds at every world of
every Kripke model $M$.

articles.title: Soundness of S4 for reflexive transitive Kripke models
articles.statement:
If the accessibility relation of
a Kripke model $M$ is reflexive and transitive, then every formula derivable in the modal logic
S4 is valid in $M$, that is, it holds at every world of $M$.

articles.title: Soundness of S5 for Kripke models with an equivalence relation
articles.statement:
If the accessibility
relation of a Kripke model $M$ is an equivalence relation, then every formula derivable in the
modal logic S5 is valid in $M$, that is, it holds at every world of $M$.

articles.title: Soundness of T for reflexive Kripke models
articles.statement:
If the accessibility relation of a Kripke
model $M$ is reflexive, then every formula derivable in the modal logic T is valid in $M$, that
is, it holds at every world of $M$.

articles.title: Soundness of modal Hilbert systems for Kripke models
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal
formulas and $M$ a Kripke model in which every formula of $\Lambda$ is valid. Then every formula
derivable in $K \oplus \Lambda$ (from the propositional axioms, the distribution axiom and the
members of $\Lambda$ by modus ponens and necessitation) is valid in $M$, that is, it holds at
every world of $M$.

articles.title: Hoare rule for nondeterministic choice
articles.statement: Nondeterministic choice is safe exactly when both branches are.

articles.title: Hoare rule of consequence
articles.statement: Strengthen the precondition and weaken the postcondition.

articles.title: Hoare triples with formula assertions as box validity
articles.statement:
Formula assertions connect Hoare verification to global PDL validity,
not just an atomic-action modality.

articles.title: Partial correctness as inclusion in the relational core
articles.statement: Partial correctness agrees with the canonical relation's core.

articles.title: Hoare triples as KAT absorption equations
articles.statement: The equivalent KAT absorption equation for verification.

articles.title: Hoare triples as KAT test inequalities
articles.statement: Hoare verification is equivalent to the KAT test inequality.

articles.title: Partial-correctness Hoare triple for PDL programs
articles.statement:
Every execution of `a` from `P` ends in `Q`, without a termination
requirement.

articles.title: PDL induction restricted to reachable states
articles.statement:
PDL induction restricted to states reachable from the initial world.
This proves `[a*](φ → [a]φ) → (φ → [a*]φ)` without assuming preservation
on unreachable states.

articles.title: Hoare rule for sequential composition
articles.statement:
Sequential verification uses the first postcondition as the second
precondition.

articles.title: Hoare invariant rule for iteration
articles.statement:
A one-step invariant holds after every finite number of iterations,
including zero, via CSLib's canonical closure-preservation theorem.

articles.title: Hoare rule for formula tests
articles.statement: A formula test requires the postcondition only where the test passes.

articles.title: Test absorption lifts through iteration
articles.statement:
Concrete relational test absorption lifts through PDL iteration,
connecting the algebraic verification equation to closure invariance.

articles.title: Loop exit absorption from a guarded-body absorption equation
articles.statement:
A guarded-body verification equation implies the loop's exit
verification equation over the same canonical relational carrier.

articles.title: Hoare invariant rule for guarded while loops
articles.statement:
The guarded-loop invariant rule is partial correctness, including
zero-step exits; it does not guarantee termination.

articles.title: While-loop rule with initialization and exit implication
articles.statement:
Verify a guarded loop using initialization, invariant preservation,
and the exit implication to the desired postcondition.

articles.title: Semantic completeness of the while-loop invariant rule
articles.statement:
The guarded-loop rule is semantically complete for arbitrary set
assertions. The witness is guarded-body reachability from `P`, independent
of `Q`; this is not a completeness claim for a syntactic assertion language.

articles.title: Guarded while loop in PDL
articles.statement:
A guarded loop in the existing PDL syntax: iterate guarded body
steps, then test that the guard is false.

articles.title: Possibility in PDL
articles.statement:
For a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$, the formula
$\langle\alpha\rangle\varphi$ is defined as $[\alpha](\varphi \to \bot) \to \bot$, that is, as
$\neg[\alpha]\neg\varphi$: possibility is the dual of necessity.

articles.title: PDL formulas
articles.statement:
The formulas of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type
of atomic action labels are the atoms $p$, falsity $\bot$, implications $\varphi \to \psi$ of
formulas, and boxes $[\alpha]\varphi$ of a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$. Formulas and
programs are defined by simultaneous induction.

articles.title: PDL model
articles.statement:
A model of propositional dynamic logic with set of worlds $W$ consists of a
binary accessibility relation $R_a$ on $W$ for each atomic action label $a$, and a valuation that
says which atoms are true at each world.

articles.title: Relation denoted by a PDL program
articles.statement:
In a model $M$, each program $\alpha$ denotes a binary
relation $R_\alpha$ on worlds: an atomic action $a$ denotes its accessibility relation $R_a$;
$(w, v) \in R_{\alpha;\beta}$ iff $(w, u) \in R_\alpha$ and $(u, v) \in R_\beta$ for some world
$u$; $R_{\alpha \cup \beta} = R_\alpha \cup R_\beta$; $R_{\alpha^*}$ is the reflexive-transitive
closure of $R_\alpha$; and $(w, v) \in R_{\varphi?}$ iff $w = v$ and $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in
$M$.

articles.title: PDL programs
articles.statement:
The programs of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type
of atomic action labels are the atomic actions $a$, sequential compositions $\alpha ; \beta$,
nondeterministic choices $\alpha \cup \beta$, iterations $\alpha^*$, and tests $\varphi?$ of a
formula $\varphi$. Programs and formulas are defined by simultaneous induction.

articles.title: Box of a choice
articles.statement:
For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and formula
$\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha \cup \beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if both
$[\alpha]\varphi$ and $[\beta]\varphi$ hold at $w$.

articles.title: Box of a sequential composition
articles.statement:
For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and
$\beta$, and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha;\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if
$[\alpha][\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$.

articles.title: Unfolding the box of an iteration
articles.statement:
For every model $M$, world $w$, program $\alpha$ and
formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at
$w$ and $[\alpha][\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$.

articles.title: Box of a test
articles.statement:
For every model $M$, world $w$ and formulas $\psi$ and $\varphi$, the formula
$[\psi?]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\psi$ holds at $w$.

articles.title: Satisfaction of PDL formulas
articles.statement:
Truth of a formula at a world $w$ of a model $M$ is defined
by recursion: an atom $p$ holds at $w$ iff the valuation of $M$ makes $p$ true at $w$; $\bot$
holds nowhere; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds at $w$ iff $\psi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\varphi$ does;
and $[\alpha]\varphi$ holds at $w$ iff $\varphi$ holds at every world $v$ with
$(w, v) \in R_\alpha$, where $R_\alpha$ is the relation denoted by $\alpha$ in $M$.

articles.title: The toggle model
articles.statement:
The PDL model whose worlds are the two Booleans $\mathsf{true}$ and
$\mathsf{false}$, with a single atomic action $a$ and a single atom $p$: the action $a$ relates
each world $s$ exactly to its negation $\lnot s$, and $p$ holds exactly at $\mathsf{true}$.

articles.title: Failure of $(a;a)\,p$ in the toggle model
articles.statement:
In the toggle model, with atomic action $a$
and atom $p$, the formula $[a;a]\,p$ is not satisfied at the world $\mathsf{false}$.

Performing $a$ twice leads from $\mathsf{false}$ back to $\mathsf{false}$, where $p$ is false.

articles.title: Relational interpretation preserves executions
articles.statement: The representation conversion preserves exactly the executions.

articles.title: Choice is interpreted by relational union
articles.statement: The interpretation of choice uses canonical union.

articles.title: Sequencing is interpreted by relational composition
articles.statement: The interpretation of sequencing uses canonical composition.

articles.title: Iteration is interpreted by reflexive-transitive closure
articles.statement:
Iteration in the canonical carrier is the same reflexive-transitive
closure as in `ProgRel`, including its identity boundary.

articles.title: Tests are interpreted by PDL satisfaction
articles.statement: Formula tests use the existing PDL satisfaction predicate.

articles.title: Relational interpretation of a PDL program
articles.statement: Interpret a PDL program in CSLib's canonical relation algebra.

articles.title: Atoms of a modal formula
articles.statement:
The set of atoms (propositional variables) occurring in a modal
formula.

articles.title: Iterated box
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k$ and a modal formula $\varphi$, the iterated box
$\Box^k \varphi$ is defined by $\Box^0 \varphi = \varphi$ and
$\Box^{k+1} \varphi = \Box\,\Box^k \varphi$.

articles.title: Negative modal formulas
articles.statement:
Negative and positive modal formulas are defined by simultaneous
recursion: no atom is negative, $\bot$ is negative, $\varphi \to \psi$ is negative if $\varphi$
is positive and $\psi$ is negative, and $\Box\varphi$ is negative if $\varphi$ is negative.

Negative formulas are closed under $\wedge$, $\vee$, $\Box$ and $\Diamond$, which are encoded
through $\to$, $\bot$ and $\Box$.

articles.title: Positive modal formulas
articles.statement:
Positive and negative modal formulas are defined by simultaneous
recursion: every atom is positive, $\bot$ is positive, $\varphi \to \psi$ is positive if
$\varphi$ is negative and $\psi$ is positive, and $\Box\varphi$ is positive if $\varphi$ is
positive.

Positive formulas are closed under $\wedge$, $\vee$, $\Box$ and $\Diamond$, which are encoded
through $\to$, $\bot$ and $\Box$.

articles.title: Sahlqvist antecedents
articles.statement:
The Sahlqvist antecedents form the smallest class of modal
formulas that contains every boxed atom $\Box^k p$ (an atom $p$ under $k \ge 0$ boxes) and every
negative formula, and is closed under $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\Diamond$.

articles.title: The B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula
articles.statement:
For every atom $p$, the instance $p \to \Box\Diamond p$
of the B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula: its antecedent $p$ is a boxed atom with zero boxes and its
consequent $\Box\Diamond p$ is positive.

articles.title: Sahlqvist implications
articles.statement:
A modal formula is a Sahlqvist implication if it is an implication
$\alpha \to \beta$ whose antecedent $\alpha$ is a Sahlqvist antecedent and whose consequent
$\beta$ is a positive formula.

articles.title: Sahlqvist formulas
articles.statement:
The Sahlqvist formulas form the smallest class of modal formulas that
contains every Sahlqvist implication, is closed under $\wedge$ and $\Box$, and contains
$\varphi \vee \psi$ whenever $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are Sahlqvist formulas with no atom in common.

The side condition on disjunction is essential: arbitrary disjunction leaves the correspondence
class. $\Diamond$ is not part of this outer closure; it belongs to the grammar of Sahlqvist
antecedents. For example, the boxed Sahlqvist implication $\Box(p \to \Box\Diamond p)$ is a
Sahlqvist formula.

articles.title: Boxing an implication chain
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms, let
$\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ be formulas (with $n \ge 0$) and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then
$\Box(\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \gamma_n \to \varphi) \to
(\Box\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \Box\gamma_n \to \Box\varphi)$
is a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: The canonical model as a CSLib model
articles.statement:
For a set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, this is the
unimodal model of CSLib's modal semantics whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of
$K \oplus \Lambda$, in which $M$ sees $N$ iff $\varphi \in N$ for every formula $\varphi$ with
$\Box\varphi \in M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $M$ iff $p \in M$.

No consistency hypothesis on $K \oplus \Lambda$ is needed here, since a CSLib model may have no
worlds.

articles.title: The canonical model
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms such that $\bot$ is not a
theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$. The canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ is the Kripke model
whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$ (there is at least one, by
Lindenbaum's lemma), in which $M$ sees $N$ iff $\varphi \in N$ for every formula $\varphi$
with $\Box\varphi \in M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $M$ iff $p \in M$.

articles.title: Worlds of the canonical model
articles.statement:
For a set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, the worlds of the
canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$: the
sets of formulas that are consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ and have no consistent proper
superset.

articles.title: Strong completeness of K
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula.
Suppose that for every Kripke model whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and
every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then
$\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in K.

articles.title: Strong completeness of S4
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula.
Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation whose
worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas
of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in S4.

articles.title: Strong completeness of S5
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula.
Suppose that for every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and
whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all
formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in
S5.

articles.title: Strong completeness of T
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula.
Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation whose worlds form a
type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$
hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in T.

articles.title: Consistency is of finite character
articles.statement:
For every set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, a set of
formulas is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ iff all its finite subsets are.

articles.title: Consistency relative to a normal modal logic
articles.statement:
For sets of formulas $\Lambda$ and
$\Gamma$, the set $\Gamma$ is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ when $\bot$ is not
deducible from $\Gamma$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Strong soundness and completeness of K
articles.statement:
For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every
modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in K if and only if $\Gamma$
locally entails $\varphi$ over all Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke
model, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S4
articles.statement:
For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every
modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S4 if and only if $\Gamma$
locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive transitive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of
every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation, with worlds in the
universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S5
articles.statement:
For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every
modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S5 if and only if $\Gamma$
locally entails $\varphi$ over Kripke models whose accessibility relation is an equivalence
relation: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every such Kripke model, with worlds in the universe of
the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Strong soundness and completeness of T
articles.statement:
For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every
modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in T if and only if $\Gamma$
locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every
Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at
which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Double-negation introduction under a box
articles.statement:
For every set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms and every
modal formula $\psi$, the formula $\Box\psi 	o \Box
eg
eg\psi$ is a theorem of the normal modal
logic $K \oplus \Lambda$, where $
eg\chi$ abbreviates $\chi 	o  ot$.

articles.title: Soundness and completeness of K
articles.statement:
A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K if and only if
$\varphi$ is valid, that is, true at every world, in every Kripke model whose worlds live in the
universe of the atoms.

articles.title: Completeness for CSLib's K
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language over
a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a
theorem of K if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$ belongs
to CSLib's semantic logic K over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib
model with worlds $W$.

articles.title: Validity in a class containing the canonical model gives derivability
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a
set of extra axioms, and let $S$ be a set of CSLib unimodal models whose worlds are the maximal
consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$. If $S$ contains the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$,
viewed as a CSLib model, and a CSLib proposition $\varphi$ holds at every world of every model in
$S$, then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of
$K \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Completeness for CSLib's S4
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language
over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is
a theorem of S4 if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$
belongs to CSLib's semantic logic S4 over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of
every CSLib model with worlds $W$ whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive.

articles.title: Completeness for CSLib's S5
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language
over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is
a theorem of S5 if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$
belongs to CSLib's semantic logic S5 over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of
every CSLib model with worlds $W$ whose accessibility relation $R$ is reflexive, transitive and
right Euclidean ($w R u$ and $w R v$ imply $u R v$).

articles.title: Completeness for CSLib's T
articles.statement:
For a CSLib unimodal proposition $\varphi$, the translation
of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system T if and only
if, for every type of worlds in the universe of the atoms, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic
T over that type, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model on that type whose
accessibility relation is reflexive.

articles.title: Soundness and completeness of S4
articles.statement:
A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S4 if and only
if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and
transitive and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.

articles.title: Soundness and completeness of S5
articles.statement:
A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S5 if and only
if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence
relation and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.

articles.title: Soundness and completeness of T
articles.statement:
A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of T if and only
if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and whose
type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.

articles.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for normal modal logics
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and
$\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every set
$\Gamma$ of modal formulas that is consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ is contained
in a set $M$ of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to
$\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

The proof applies the Teichmüller–Tukey lemma: consistency is a property of finite character.

articles.title: Existence lemma
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ the
normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, $M$ a canonical world, that is, a set of
modal formulas maximal among the sets consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, and
$\varphi$ a modal formula. If $\Box\varphi \notin M$, then there is a canonical world $N$ with
$\varphi \notin N$ that is accessible from $M$ in the canonical relation: every $\psi$ with
$\Box\psi \in M$ lies in $N$.

articles.title: Discharging a list of hypotheses
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas,
$\varphi$ a modal formula and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ a list of modal formulas. If $\varphi$
is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n\}$ in the normal modal logic K
extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, then
$\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots)$ is a local consequence of
$\Gamma$ in the same logic.

articles.title: Local semantic consequence over a class of Kripke models
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a class of Kripke
models, given as a predicate on models. A set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas locally entails a formula
$\varphi$ over $C$ when, for every Kripke model $M$ in $C$ whose type of worlds lies in the
universe of the atoms and every world $w$ of $M$, if every formula of $\Gamma$ is satisfied at $w$
in $M$, then $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$.

articles.title: Soundness for CSLib's K
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation
of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system K, then, for
every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic K: it holds at every world of every
CSLib unimodal model on that type.

articles.title: Validity of the translation gives membership in CSLib's logic
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a class of CSLib
unimodal models on a type of worlds and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Suppose that, if
the type of worlds is nonempty, the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is
valid in the Kripke model of every model in $S$. Then $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic
of $S$: it holds at every world of every model in $S$.

articles.title: Maximal consistent sets of modal formulas are deductively closed
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set
of modal formulas and $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent
relative to the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every formula that is a
local consequence of $M$ in that logic belongs to $M$.

articles.title: Iterated modus ponens in maximal consistent sets
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal
formulas, $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to the
normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, and $\varphi$ and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$
modal formulas. If $\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots) \in M$
and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n \in M$, then $\varphi \in M$.

articles.title: Soundness for CSLib's S4
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation
of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system S4, then, for
every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic S4: it holds at every world of every
CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive.

articles.title: Soundness for CSLib's S5
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation
of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system S5, then, for
every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic S5: it holds at every world of every
CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation $R$ is reflexive, transitive and
Euclidean ($R(w, u)$ and $R(w, v)$ imply $R(u, v)$).

articles.title: Soundness for CSLib's T
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation
of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system T, then, for
every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic T: it holds at every world of every
CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive.

articles.title: Completeness relative to the canonical model
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas
such that $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$, let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and
$\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ holds at every world of the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$
at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Deducibility from maximal consistent extensions
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal
formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ belongs to every maximal
$(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set that contains $\Gamma$, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in
$K \oplus \Lambda$.

articles.title: Kripke to CSLib and back is the identity
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a Kripke model on a nonempty type of
worlds. Converting $k$ to a CSLib unimodal model and converting that model back to a Kripke model
gives $k$.

articles.title: Kripke model of a CSLib model
articles.statement:
For a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on a nonempty type of worlds,
the associated Kripke model has the same worlds, the binary accessibility relation of $m$ as its
accessibility relation, and the valuation of $m$ as its valuation.

articles.title: Translation of CSLib's modal propositions
articles.statement:
CSLib's unimodal propositions are translated into
modal formulas in the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis by recursion, writing $\varphi'$ for the
translation of $\varphi$: an atom $p$ goes to $p$, falsehood to $\bot$, $\neg\varphi$ to
$\varphi' \to \bot$, $\varphi \lor \psi$ to $(\varphi' \to \bot) \to \psi'$, and the diamond
(the unimodal triangle) applied to $\varphi$ goes to $\Diamond\varphi'$, that is, to
$\Box(\varphi' \to \bot) \to \bot$.

articles.title: The canonical accessibility relation
articles.statement:
For a set $\Lambda$ of modal formulas and maximal
$(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent sets $M$ and $N$ (worlds of the canonical model), $M$ is related to
$N$ iff every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$ belongs to $N$.

articles.title: Model existence for K
articles.statement:
For every K-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a
Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every
formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Model existence from the canonical model
articles.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $C$
a class of Kripke models whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, such that $C$ contains the
canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ whenever $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$. Then
every $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set $\Gamma$ of formulas is satisfiable in $C$: some model in
$C$ has a world at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

This is strong completeness in satisfiability form. The converse needs every model in $C$ to
validate $\Lambda$; for K, T, S4 and S5 it is soundness.

articles.title: Model existence for S4
articles.statement:
For every S4-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a
reflexive transitive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it
at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Model existence for S5
articles.statement:
For every S5-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a
Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence and whose worlds lie in the universe
of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Model existence for T
articles.statement:
For every T-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a
reflexive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which
every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

articles.title: Truth lemma
articles.statement: A formula holds at a world of the canonical model iff it belongs to it.

articles.title: The translation preserves satisfaction
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a CSLib unimodal model on a nonempty type
of worlds, $w$ a world and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Then the translation of $\varphi$
into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis holds at $w$ in the Kripke model of $m$ if and only if
$\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $m$.

articles.title: The reverse translation preserves satisfaction
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a Kripke model, $w$ a world
and $\varphi$ a modal formula in the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis. Then $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $k$
if and only if its translation into a CSLib unimodal proposition holds at $w$ in the CSLib model
associated with $k$.

Together with the preservation of satisfaction by the forward translation and the two model round
trips, this shows that the two presentations have the same unimodal semantics.

articles.title: Round trip from CSLib models through Kripke models
articles.statement:
For a nonempty type of worlds $W$,
converting a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on $W$ into a Kripke model and then back into a CSLib
unimodal model returns $m$: a unimodal frame is determined by its binary accessibility relation.

articles.title: The CSLib unimodal model of a Kripke model
articles.statement:
A Kripke model $k$ on worlds $W$ gives the
CSLib unimodal model on $W$ whose frame is the unimodal frame built from the accessibility
relation of $k$ and whose valuation is the valuation of $k$.

articles.title: Translation of modal formulas into CSLib propositions
articles.statement:
Each modal formula built from
atoms, $\bot$, $\to$ and $\Box$ is translated into a CSLib unimodal proposition by recursion:
an atom $p$ goes to the atom $p$, $\bot$ goes to false, $\varphi \to \psi$ goes to
$\neg\varphi' \lor \psi'$, and $\Box\varphi$ goes to $\neg\Diamond\neg\varphi'$, where
$\varphi'$ and $\psi'$ are the translations of $\varphi$ and $\psi$ and $\Diamond$ is the
possibility operator of CSLib's unimodal language.

articles.title: Validity agrees with its CSLib translation
articles.statement:
A modal formula $\varphi$ is
valid in a Kripke model $k$ (true at every world of $k$) if and only if its translation into a
CSLib unimodal proposition is satisfied at every world of the CSLib unimodal model associated
with $k$.

articles.title: Modal formulas are bisimulation-invariant under the standard translation
articles.statement:
For every
modal formula $\varphi$, its standard translation $ST_x(\varphi)$ (the first-order formula over
the modal language whose single variable $x$ stands for the current world) is
bisimulation-invariant: for all Kripke models $M$ and $N$, every bisimulation $Z$ between $M$
and $N$ and all worlds $w$ of $M$ and $v$ of $N$ with $Z(w, v)$, the formula $ST_x(\varphi)$
holds in $M$ at $x = w$ if and only if it holds in $N$ at $x = v$.

articles.title: Bisimulation-invariant formulas
articles.statement:
A first-order formula $\alpha$ over the modal language,
with one variable $x$ and no other free variables, is bisimulation-invariant if for all Kripke
models $M$ and $N$ over the same atoms, every bisimulation $Z$ between $M$ and $N$ and all
worlds $w$ of $M$ and $v$ of $N$ with $Z(w, v)$, the formula $\alpha$ holds in $M$ (viewed as
a structure for the modal language) at $x = w$ if and only if it holds in $N$ at $x = v$.

articles.title: First-order language of Kripke frames
articles.statement: The first-order language of frames: no function symbols, one binary relation `R`.

articles.title: Relation symbols of the frame language
articles.statement:
The relation symbols of the first-order frame
language, indexed by arity: a single binary symbol $R$ for accessibility, and no symbols of any
other arity.

articles.title: A frame as a first-order structure
articles.statement:
A binary relation $r$ on a set $W$ (a bare Kripke
frame) makes $W$ a structure for the frame language, in which the accessibility symbol $R$ is
interpreted as $r$: $R(w, w')$ holds if and only if $r(w, w')$.

articles.title: A Kripke model as a first-order structure
articles.statement:
A Kripke model $M$ with set of worlds $W$
makes $W$ a structure for the modal language: the accessibility symbol $R$ is interpreted as
the accessibility relation of $M$, and the predicate $P_a$ for an atom $a$ holds at exactly
the worlds where $a$ is true under the valuation of $M$.

articles.title: The first-order modal language
articles.statement:
For a set of atoms, the first-order language of modal
logic has no function symbols; its relation symbols are a binary symbol $R$ (accessibility)
and a unary symbol $P_a$ for each atom $a$.

articles.title: Relation symbols of the modal first-order language
articles.statement:
Relation symbols of the modal first-order language: accessibility `R` (binary) and a
unary predicate `P_a` for each atom `a`.

articles.title: Correctness of the standard translation
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a Kripke model with set of worlds
$W$, viewed as a structure for the modal language. For every $n$, every term $t$ of the modal
language in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, every modal formula $\varphi$ and every
assignment of worlds in $W$ to $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, the standard translation of $\varphi$
with $n$ variables in scope and current-world term $t$ holds in $M$ under this assignment if
and only if $\varphi$ is satisfied in $M$ at the world that $t$ denotes under the
assignment.

articles.title: Standard translation
articles.statement:
For $n$ variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ in scope and a term $t$
of the modal language for the current world, the standard translation $ST_t(\varphi)$ of a
modal formula $\varphi$ is the first-order formula over the modal language in these variables
defined by recursion on $\varphi$: $ST_t(a) = P_a(t)$ for an atom $a$; $ST_t(\bot) = \bot$;
$ST_t(\varphi \to \psi) = ST_t(\varphi) \to ST_t(\psi)$; and
$ST_t(\Box \varphi) = \forall x_n \, (R(t, x_n) \to ST_{x_n}(\varphi))$, where $x_n$ is a fresh
variable and $ST_{x_n}(\varphi)$ is taken with $n + 1$ variables in scope.

articles.title: Group function symbols
articles.statement:
The function symbols of the first-order language of groups,
graded by arity, are a constant symbol for the identity (arity $0$), a symbol for inversion
(arity $1$) and a symbol for multiplication (arity $2$); there are no others.

articles.title: The function symbols of the language of groups
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the
$n$-ary function symbols of the first-order language of groups are exactly the group function
symbols of arity $n$.

articles.title: The language of groups has no relation symbols
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the
first-order language of groups has no $n$-ary relation symbols.

articles.title: Inversion in the canonical structure
articles.statement:
For every group $G$ and every one-element tuple
$(x_0)$ of elements of $G$, the inversion symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the
canonical structure on $G$, sends $(x_0)$ to $x_0^{-1}$.

articles.title: Multiplication in the canonical structure
articles.statement:
For every group $G$ and every pair
$(x_0, x_1)$ of elements of $G$, the multiplication symbol of the language of groups,
interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, sends $(x_0, x_1)$ to $x_0 x_1$.

articles.title: The identity in the canonical structure
articles.statement:
For every group $G$, the identity constant
symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, takes the value
$1$ at the empty tuple, where $1$ is the identity of $G$.

articles.title: The canonical structure on a group
articles.statement:
For a group $G$, the canonical structure on $G$ for
the first-order language of groups interprets the identity constant as the identity $1$ of $G$,
inversion as $x \mapsto x^{-1}$ and multiplication as $(x, y) \mapsto xy$; there are no
relation symbols to interpret.

articles.title: The first-order language of groups
articles.statement:
The first-order language of groups has the group
function symbols (a constant for the identity, a unary symbol for inversion and a binary symbol
for multiplication) as its function symbols and no relation symbols.

articles.title: Morley's categoricity theorem
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a first-order language with at most countably
many symbols, and let $T$ be a complete $L$-theory all of whose models are infinite. Call $T$
$\kappa$-categorical if any two models of $T$ of cardinality $\kappa$ are isomorphic. If $T$ is
$\kappa$-categorical for some uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, then $T$ is $\mu$-categorical for
every uncountable cardinal $\mu$.

## Sources

- M. Ramsey, *Morley's Categoricity Theorem* (UChicago VIGRE REU 2010), Corollary 7.3. https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/VIGRE/VIGRE2010/REUPapers/RamseyN.pdf. Problem `morley_categoricity_theorem` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Conjunction of formulas
articles.statement:
For formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the conjunction
$\varphi \wedge \psi$ is the formula $\neg(\varphi \to \neg\psi)$.

articles.title: Extending an environment
articles.statement:
An environment is a map $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ that
assigns a real number to each de Bruijn index. For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the extension of $e$ by $x$
sends index $0$ to $x$ and index $i + 1$ to $e(i)$ for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Evaluation of terms
articles.statement:
Given an environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the value of a
term in $\mathbb{R}$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable with de Bruijn index $i$ has
value $e(i)$, the integer constant $k$ has value $k$, and the value of a sum, product or negation
of terms is the sum, product or negation in $\mathbb{R}$ of the values of its parts.

articles.title: Existential quantification of formulas
articles.statement:
For a formula $\varphi$, the formula
$\exists \varphi$ is $\neg \forall \neg \varphi$; it binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$.

articles.title: Formulas of the language of ordered rings
articles.statement:
Formulas are built from the atomic formulas
$s < t$ and $s = t$, for terms $s$ and $t$, and falsity $\bot$, by implication $\varphi \to \psi$
and universal quantification $\forall \varphi$, which binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$.
Negation, truth, disjunction, conjunction and existential quantification are defined from these.

articles.title: A real number is a square exactly when it is nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every environment
$e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the formula $\exists x.\ x \cdot x = a$ holds under $e$ if and
only if the formula $\neg(a < 0)$ holds under $e$. In the first formula the bound variable $x$ is
de Bruijn index $0$ and $a$ is index $1$; in the second $a$ is index $0$; in both, $a$ denotes
$e(0)$. Thus $e(0)$ is a square in $\mathbb{R}$ exactly when $e(0) \ge 0$.

This checks the semantics and the de Bruijn convention against a known fact.

## Sources

- Tarski, 'A Decision Method for Elementary Algebra and Geometry' (1951); Collins, 'Quantifier elimination for real closed fields by cylindrical algebraic decomposition' (1975); Mahboubi, 'Programming and certifying a CAD algorithm in the Coq system' (2006); Cohen and Mahboubi, 'Formal proofs in real algebraic geometry: from ordered fields to quantifier elimination' (2012). Problem `rcf_quantifier_elimination` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Quantifier elimination preserves truth
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier elimination map
on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$ and every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$,
the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds
in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$.

Together with the statement that $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ is always quantifier free, this is
Tarski's quantifier elimination theorem, stated for $\mathbb{R}$.

## Sources

- Tarski, 'A Decision Method for Elementary Algebra and Geometry' (1951); Collins, 'Quantifier elimination for real closed fields by cylindrical algebraic decomposition' (1975); Mahboubi, 'Programming and certifying a CAD algorithm in the Coq system' (2006); Cohen and Mahboubi, 'Formal proofs in real algebraic geometry: from ordered fields to quantifier elimination' (2012). Problem `rcf_quantifier_elimination` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Satisfaction of formulas over the reals
articles.statement:
Let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be an
environment. Whether a formula holds under $e$ is defined by recursion on the formula: $s < t$
holds when the value of $s$ under $e$ is less than the value of $t$ under $e$; $s = t$ holds when
these values are equal; $\bot$ never holds; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds when $\varphi$ holding under
$e$ implies $\psi$ holding under $e$; and $\forall \varphi$ holds when, for every
$x \in \mathbb{R}$, $\varphi$ holds under the extension of $e$ by $x$.

articles.title: Quantifier elimination yields quantifier-free formulas
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier
elimination map on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ is
quantifier free.

## Sources

- Tarski, 'A Decision Method for Elementary Algebra and Geometry' (1951); Collins, 'Quantifier elimination for real closed fields by cylindrical algebraic decomposition' (1975); Mahboubi, 'Programming and certifying a CAD algorithm in the Coq system' (2006); Cohen and Mahboubi, 'Formal proofs in real algebraic geometry: from ordered fields to quantifier elimination' (2012). Problem `rcf_quantifier_elimination` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Quantifier-free formulas
articles.statement:
A formula is quantifier free if it contains no universal
quantifier $\forall$.

articles.title: Negation of a formula
articles.statement:
The negation $\neg\varphi$ of a formula $\varphi$ is the formula
$\varphi \to \bot$.

articles.title: Disjunction of formulas
articles.statement:
The disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of formulas $\varphi$ and
$\psi$ is the formula $\neg\varphi \to \psi$.

articles.title: Quantifier elimination over the reals
articles.statement:
Quantifier elimination is a map sending each formula
$\varphi$ of the language of ordered rings to a formula $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$, subject to
two requirements: $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ is quantifier free, and for every environment
$e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ assigning a real number to each variable,
$\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ does.

The formula $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ may mention additional variables, but only vacuously.

## Sources

- Tarski, 'A Decision Method for Elementary Algebra and Geometry' (1951); Collins, 'Quantifier elimination for real closed fields by cylindrical algebraic decomposition' (1975); Mahboubi, 'Programming and certifying a CAD algorithm in the Coq system' (2006); Cohen and Mahboubi, 'Formal proofs in real algebraic geometry: from ordered fields to quantifier elimination' (2012). Problem `rcf_quantifier_elimination` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Terms of the language of ordered rings
articles.statement:
Terms are built from variables $x_i$, one for
each natural number $i$ (a de Bruijn index), and integer constants $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, using
addition $s + t$, multiplication $s \cdot t$ and negation $-t$.

articles.title: The true formula
articles.statement:
The formula $\top$ is the negation $\neg\bot$ of falsity, that is, the
formula $\bot \to \bot$.

articles.title: Algebraic part of a set
articles.statement:
For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the algebraic part
$X^{\mathrm{alg}}$ of $X$ is the union of all connected, infinite semialgebraic sets $Y$ with
$Y \subseteq X$.

The source takes the union of the connected, positive-dimensional semialgebraic subsets of $X$;
for connected semialgebraic sets, being infinite is equivalent to being positive-dimensional.

articles.title: Wilkie's conjecture for the real exponential field
articles.statement:
Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be
definable in $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$. Then there is a polynomial $f$ in two variables with real
coefficients such that the following holds for all natural numbers $g$ and $H$. Let
$X^{\mathrm{trans}}(g, H)$ be the set of points $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of the transcendental part
$X^{\mathrm{trans}}$ of $X$ whose coordinates are all algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, such that the
field $\mathbb{Q}(x) = \mathbb{Q}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ satisfies $[\mathbb{Q}(x) : \mathbb{Q}] \le g$
and the height $H(x)$ of $x$, the maximum of the absolute multiplicative Weil heights of
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ (taken to be $0$ when $n = 0$), satisfies $H(x) \le H$. Then
$X^{\mathrm{trans}}(g, H)$ is finite and has at most $f(g, \log H)$ elements, where $\log 0$ is
taken to be $0$.

This is Corollary 1 of the source.

## Sources

- G. Binyamini, D. Novikov, and B. Zak, `Wilkie's conjecture for Pfaffian structures`, Annals of Math, 199 (2) 2024. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_wilkies_conjecture` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Points of bounded degree and height
articles.statement:
For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and natural
numbers $g$ and $H$, the set $X(g, H)$ consists of the points $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n) \in X$ whose
coordinates are all algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, such that the field
$\mathbb{Q}(x) = \mathbb{Q}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ satisfies $[\mathbb{Q}(x) : \mathbb{Q}] \le g$ and
the height $H(x)$ of $x$, the maximum of the absolute multiplicative Weil heights of
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ (taken to be $0$ when $n = 0$), satisfies $H(x) \le H$.

articles.title: Function symbols of the language of exponentiation
articles.statement:
The function symbols of the language
of exponentiation, sorted by arity: there is exactly one, the unary symbol $\exp$, and there are
none of any other arity.

articles.title: Language of rings with exponentiation
articles.statement:
The first-order language whose function symbols
are those of the language of rings, namely the binary symbols $+$ and $\cdot$, the unary symbol
$-$ and the constants $0$ and $1$, together with the unary symbol $\exp$ of the language of
exponentiation; it has no relation symbols.

articles.title: Language of exponentiation
articles.statement:
The first-order language with a single function symbol, the
unary symbol $\exp$, and no relation symbols.

articles.title: Height of a point
articles.statement:
For $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the height $H(a)$ is the
maximum of the absolute multiplicative Weil heights of the coordinates $a_1, \dots, a_n$. A
coordinate that is not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ counts with height $1$, and for $n = 0$ the
height is $0$.

articles.title: Definable sets of the real exponential field
articles.statement:
A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is definable
in $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$ if it is definable, with parameters from $\mathbb{R}$, in the real numbers
viewed as a structure for the language of rings with exponentiation, where the ring symbols have
their usual meaning and $\exp$ is interpreted as the real exponential function.

articles.title: Semialgebraic set
articles.statement:
A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is semialgebraic if it is definable,
with parameters from $\mathbb{R}$, in the real numbers viewed as a structure for the language of
rings.

articles.title: Transcendental part of a set
articles.statement:
For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the transcendental
part of $X$ is $X^{\mathrm{trans}} := X \setminus X^{\mathrm{alg}}$, where $X^{\mathrm{alg}}$ is
the algebraic part of $X$.

articles.title: Cut admissibility in the pinned bundle with list tails

articles.title: Cut-free original proof from an explicit list presentation

Every original CLL proof has a cut-free original proof of the same sequent.

Given a list of `ʔ`-propositions `Γ`, transforms a proof of `Γ + Γ + Δ` into a proof of `Γ + Δ`
via contraction.

articles.statement: Transporting a conclusion preserves cut-freeness.

articles.title: Cut-freeness of a proof
articles.statement: A proof is cut-free if it does not contain any applications of rule cut.

articles.title: Unit rule $1$ of the cut-free system
articles.statement: Rule `1` for CF.

articles.title: Second plus rule of the cut-free system
articles.statement: Rule `⊕₂` for CF.

articles.statement: Rule `⊕₁` for CF.

articles.statement: Rule `⅋` for CF.

articles.statement: Proofs in the CF inference system.

articles.title: Dereliction rule of the cut-free system
articles.statement: Rule `?` (dereliction) for CF.

articles.statement: Recursor for cut-free proofs: never sees the `cut` case.

articles.title: Rewriting the conclusion of a cut-free proof
articles.statement:
Rewrites the conclusion of a cut-free proof.
If `h` is omitted, tries to prove the equality using `grind only [multiset]`.

articles.title: Locating a head proposition in a sum of sequents
articles.statement:
Given `a ::ₘ Γ = (Δ : Sequent) + Θ`, locate `a` in either `Δ` or `Θ` and
erase it from that summand, returning the residual list.

articles.title: Case split on an equation of cons sequents
articles.statement:
Distinguish a principal selected occurrence using decidable equality.
Given `a ::ₘ Γ = b ::ₘ Δ`, either `a = b` and `Γ = Δ`, or `a ≠ b` and the propositions are swapped:
`Γ = b ::ₘ Λ` and `Δ = a ::ₘ Λ` for some `Λ`.
The tail `Δ` can be an arbitrary multiset; the residual list is obtained from `Γ`.

articles.title: Splitting replicated copies across a sum of sequents
articles.statement:
Given `Multiset.replicate n a + Γ = (Δ : Sequent) + Θ`, split the `n` copies of `a`
between `Δ` and `Θ`, returning counts `k` and `l` and residual lists.

articles.title: Case split of a cons against replicated copies
articles.statement:
Given `Multiset.replicate n a + Γ = b ::ₘ Δ`, either the head `b` is one of the
`n` copies of `a` (so `b = a` and the tail is `replicate (n-1) a + Γ`), or `b` belongs to
`Γ` (so `Δ = Multiset.replicate n a + Γ'` where `Γ = b ::ₘ Γ'`).
The tail `Δ` can be an arbitrary multiset; the residual list is obtained from `Γ`.

articles.title: Tensor rule of the cut-free system
articles.statement: Rule `⊗` for CF.

articles.title: Top rule of the cut-free system
articles.statement: Rule `⊤` for CF.

articles.title: Weakening by a list of question-mark propositions
articles.statement:
Given a list of `ʔ`-propositions `Γ`, transforms a cut-free proof of `Δ` into a proof of `Γ + Δ`
via weakening.

articles.title: Weakening rule of the cut-free system
articles.statement: Rule `?` (weaken) for CF.

articles.title: With rule of the cut-free system
articles.statement: Rule `&` for CF.

articles.statement: Checking a list context agrees with checking its multiset coercion.

articles.title: A cons sequent is all question marks iff its head and tail are
articles.statement: A cons sequent consists of `ʔ`-propositions exactly when its head and tail do.

articles.title: A question-mark head does not change the all-question-mark property
articles.statement: Adding a `ʔ`-proposition preserves and reflects `allQuest`.

articles.title: Empty sequent consists of question-mark propositions
articles.statement: The empty sequent consists of `ʔ`-propositions.

articles.title: Check that every proposition in a list is a why-not proposition
articles.statement: Checks that all propositions in a list are question marks (`ʔ`).

articles.statement: Conclusion transport preserves the pinned Boolean cut-free check.

articles.title: Height of a classical linear logic proof
articles.statement: Height of a proof.

articles.statement: A sequent containing a `!`-proposition cannot satisfy `allQuest`.

articles.title: Conclusion transport preserves proof height
articles.statement: Transporting a conclusion preserves proof height.

articles.title: List representative of a submultiset by scanning a list
articles.statement:
Compute a list representative of a submultiset by scanning a supplied list.
The resulting list preserves the order of the selected occurrences in the supplied list.

articles.title: Cut admissibility for a bang proposition
articles.statement:
Cut a bang proposition by commuting through its supplying proof to an axiom or promotion.
At promotion, delegates to `questMulticut` with one selected occurrence.

articles.title: Core cut admissibility procedure on list sequents
articles.statement:
The core cut admissibility implementation: given decidable atom equality and explicit
list sequents, combine cut-free proofs of dual distinguished propositions into a cut-free
proof of the sum of their residual sequents. Recurses on proposition size.

articles.title: Cut admissibility for non-exponential propositions
articles.statement:
Cut admissibility for non-exponential propositions: uses height induction on the
sum of premise heights, with commuting cases for non-principal rules.
Only callable when neither `a` nor `a⫠` is a question mark.

articles.title: Proposition-size induction step for cut admissibility
articles.statement:
The proposition-size induction step for cut admissibility.
Dispatches to `bangCutAdm`, `questCutAdm`, or `cutAdmNonExponential` depending on
the top-level connective.

articles.title: Cut admissibility for cut-free classical linear logic proofs
articles.statement:
Public entry point for cut admissibility: given cut-free proofs of `a ::ₘ Γ` and
`a⫠ ::ₘ Δ`, produce a cut-free proof of `(Γ : Sequent) + Δ`.

articles.title: Cut elimination by structural recursion on the proof
articles.statement:
Compute cut-free proofs by structural recursion on the original (possibly
non-cut-free) proof. Each case recursively normalises the premises, then uses
`cutAdm` at each cut. The list `Γ` is the explicit sequent for the current subgoal.

articles.title: List-based cut elimination in the source calculus
articles.statement: List-based cut elimination with the concrete list presentation explicit.

articles.title: Cut elimination with a noncomputable list presentation
articles.statement: Cut elimination, using a noncomputable list presentation.

articles.title: Reduction of a cut between matching principal rules
articles.statement:
Reduce a pair of principal rules whose conclusions match the cut proposition.
Every recursive call is on a proper subproposition of the original cut proposition,
so termination is guaranteed by proposition size.

articles.title: Principal shapes of a cut-free proof at the cut proposition
articles.statement:
The shape of a cut-free proof when the cut proposition is in principal position.
Each constructor corresponds to a rule whose conclusion matches the cut proposition.
Axioms are handled separately in `cutStep`. Tensor carries explicit presentations
of both premises' residual contexts.

articles.title: Cut step exposing a principal rule or commuting the cut
articles.statement:
Decompose a cut against a cut-free proof: either expose a principal rule matching
the cut proposition, or commute the cut through one inference (non-principal case).
Every recursive call is on a strictly shorter supplying derivation.

articles.title: List presentations of two summands from a supplied list
articles.statement: Present both summands using only the supplied list.

articles.title: List presentation of a tail without choosing a representative
articles.statement: Present a tail without choosing a multiset representative.

articles.title: Question-mark cut via the bang case, duality and exchange
articles.statement:
Reverse the exponential cut orientation using `bangCutAdm`, duality, and exchange.
This is a wrapper, not a recursive call that swaps premises at the same measure.

articles.title: Splitting a selected occurrence against a rule head
articles.statement: Split a selected occurrence against a rule head; the rule tail can be a multiset.

articles.title: Cut admissibility at a fixed proposition
articles.statement:
Cut admissibility at a fixed proposition `a`: for any list sequents `Γ`, `Δ`, given
cut-free proofs of `a ::ₘ Γ` and `a⫠ ::ₘ Δ`, produce a cut-free proof of
`(Γ : Sequent Atom) + Δ`.

articles.title: Cut admissibility below a size bound
articles.statement:
The outer induction hypothesis for cut admissibility: for all propositions `a` with
`sizeOf a < bound`, cut is admissible at `a`.

articles.title: Axiom case of the exponential multicut
articles.statement:
Ax case for `questMulticut`: the selected dual question mark is one of the copies of `a⫠`.
This isolates the recursive branch from the plain-term outer proof.

articles.title: Exponential multicut against replicated question marks
articles.statement:
Exponential/multicut helper: given `p : CF⇓(a ::ₘ Γ)` (the "substitutend") and
`q : CF⇓(Multiset.replicate n (ʔ(a⫠)) + Δ)` (the "supply" with `n` selected dual question marks),
produce `CF⇓((Γ : Sequent) + Δ)`.

articles.title: Splitting replicated question marks across two summands
articles.statement: Split replicated question marks across two arbitrary multiset summands.

articles.title: Locating a selected question mark or a residual head
articles.statement: Locate a selected question mark or a residual head using `Sequent.splitReplicateCons`.

articles.title: Abstract Gödel–Rosser incompleteness theorem
Gödel's second incompleteness theorem, abstract Hilbert–Bernays–Löb form
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$
be a set of sentences with an implication $\to$, a sentence $\bot$, a negation satisfying
$\neg A = (A \to \bot)$ for all $A$, and a provability operator
$\Box : \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{L}$.
Let $U \vdash A$ be a relation between theories $U \subseteq \mathcal{L}$ and sentences
$A \in \mathcal{L}$ such that for every theory $U$ and all sentences $A$, $B$, $C$:
$U \vdash A \to (B \to A)$, $U \vdash (A \to (B \to C)) \to ((A \to B) \to (A \to C))$, and if
$U \vdash A \to B$ and $U \vdash A$, then $U \vdash B$. Let $T_0$ and $T$ be theories such that
$T_0 \vdash A$ implies $T \vdash A$ for every $A$, and suppose there is a sentence $G$ with
$T_0 \vdash G \to \neg \Box G$ and $T_0 \vdash \neg \Box G \to G$. Suppose that for all sentences
$A$, $B$: if $T \vdash A$, then $T \vdash \Box A$; $T \vdash \Box(A \to B) \to (\Box A \to \Box B)$;
and $T \vdash \Box A \to \Box \Box A$. Let $\mathrm{Con} = \neg \Box \bot$. If $T \nvdash \bot$,
then $T \nvdash \mathrm{Con}$.

The derivability conditions and the fixed point are assumed rather than derived from a concrete
encoding of first-order arithmetic.

Proof: Derive the needed implicational combinators from K and S, apply D1–D3 to the Gödel
fixed point $G$, and contrapose $\Box G \to \Box \bot$. This is the Hilbert–Bernays–Löb route
of Hilbert–Bernays (1939) and Löb (1955), as presented by Boolos, Ch. 3, and Smith, Ch. 33.

## Sources

- Kurt Gödel, *Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze der Principia Mathematica und verwandter Systeme I*, Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik 38 (1931), 173–198; Martin H. Löb, *Solution of a problem of Leon Henkin*, Journal of Symbolic Logic 20 (1955), 115–118.

articles.title: Adding a why-not proposition keeps a sequent all why-not
articles.statement:
For every CLL proposition $a$
and every CLL sequent $\Delta$, every proposition of the sequent $?a, \Delta$ has the form $?b$
for some $b$ if and only if every proposition of $\Delta$ does.

articles.title: Promotion in a translated hypothesis context
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map atoms to CLL propositions, let
$\Gamma$ be a multiset of propositional formulas, and write $?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ for the CLL
sequent of the propositions $?((B^\circ)^\perp)$, one for each $B \in \Gamma$ counted with
multiplicity, where $B^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $B$ with atoms translated by $f$. For
every CLL proposition $a$, if the sequent $\vdash a, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ is provable in CLL,
then so is $\vdash !a, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$.

articles.title: The atom map sending $\bot$ to $0$
articles.statement:
For a type of atoms with a distinguished atom $\bot$
and decidable equality, this is the map from atoms to CLL propositions that sends $\bot$ to the
additive unit $0$ and every other atom $a$ to the CLL atom $a$.

articles.title: Contraction of a translated hypothesis context
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map atoms to CLL propositions,
let $\Gamma$ be a multiset of propositional formulas, and write $?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ for the
CLL sequent of the propositions $?((B^\circ)^\perp)$, one for each $B \in \Gamma$ counted with
multiplicity, where $B^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $B$ with atoms translated by $f$. For
every CLL sequent $\Delta$, if $\vdash ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}, \Delta$ is
provable in CLL, then so is $\vdash ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}, \Delta$.

articles.title: Cut of a translated hypothesis context against a closed proof
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map atoms to CLL
propositions, let $\Gamma$ be a multiset of propositional formulas, and write
$?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ for the CLL sequent of the propositions $?((B^\circ)^\perp)$, one for
each $B \in \Gamma$ counted with multiplicity, where $B^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $B$
with atoms translated by $f$. For all CLL propositions $a$ and $c$, if
$\vdash a, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ is provable in CLL and there is a CLL proof of
$\vdash a^\perp, c$, then $\vdash c, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ is provable in CLL.

articles.title: Cut within a translated hypothesis context
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map atoms to CLL propositions, let
$\Gamma$ be a multiset of propositional formulas, and write $?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ for the CLL
sequent of the propositions $?((B^\circ)^\perp)$, one for each $B \in \Gamma$ counted with
multiplicity, where $B^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $B$ with atoms translated by $f$. For
all CLL propositions $a$ and $c$, if both $\vdash a, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ and
$\vdash a^\perp, c, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ are provable in CLL, then so is
$\vdash c, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$.

articles.title: Girard's translation preserves provability
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map atoms to CLL propositions and
write $B^\circ$ for Girard's translation of a propositional formula $B$ with atoms translated by
$f$. Let $T$ be a propositional theory such that the one-formula sequent $\vdash B^\circ$ is
provable in CLL for every $B \in T$. If $\Gamma$ is a finite set of propositional formulas and
$\Gamma \vdash A$ has a natural-deduction derivation (in minimal propositional logic) using the
axioms of $T$, then the CLL sequent $\vdash A^\circ, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ is provable, where
$?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ consists of the propositions $?((B^\circ)^\perp)$, one for each
$B \in \Gamma$.

articles.title: Ex falso translates to a CLL theorem
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map atoms to CLL propositions and send the
atom $\bot$ to the additive unit $0$. Then for every propositional formula $B$, the one-formula
CLL sequent $\vdash (\bot \to B)^\circ$ is provable, where $(\cdot)^\circ$ is Girard's
translation with atoms translated by $f$.

The translation $(\bot \to B)^\circ$ is the par of $?\top$ and $B^\circ$, which is provable by
the $\top$ rule.

articles.title: Translated hypotheses are provable from their context
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map atoms to CLL
propositions, let $\Gamma$ be a multiset of propositional formulas, and write
$?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ for the CLL sequent of the propositions $?((B^\circ)^\perp)$, one for
each $B \in \Gamma$ counted with multiplicity, where $B^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $B$
with atoms translated by $f$. For every propositional formula $A \in \Gamma$, the sequent
