$\vdash A^\circ, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ is provable in CLL.

articles.title: Girard's translation of a reusable hypothesis
articles.statement:
Given a map $f$ from atoms to CLL
propositions and a propositional formula $A$, this is the CLL proposition $?((A^\circ)^\perp)$,
where $A^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $A$ with atoms translated by $f$ and $(\cdot)^\perp$
is linear negation.

articles.title: Translated hypotheses of a context
articles.statement:
Given a map $f$ from propositional atoms to CLL
propositions and a multiset $\Gamma$ of propositional formulas, $?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$ is the CLL
sequent consisting of the propositions $?\big((A^\circ)^\perp\big)$ for $A \in \Gamma$, counted
with multiplicity, where $A^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $A$ with atoms translated by $f$.

articles.title: Theorems of intuitionistic logic translate to CLL theorems
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map propositional atoms
to CLL propositions and send the atom $\bot$ to the additive unit $0$. If a propositional formula
$A$ is derivable in natural deduction from the empty context in intuitionistic propositional
logic (no axioms other than ex falso $\bot \to B$ for every formula $B$), then the one-sided CLL
sequent $\vdash A^\circ$ is provable, where $A^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $A$ with atoms
translated by $f$.

articles.title: Theorems of minimal logic translate to CLL theorems
articles.statement:
For every map $f$ from propositional
atoms to CLL propositions, if a propositional formula $A$ is derivable in natural deduction from
the empty context with no axioms (minimal logic), then the one-sided CLL sequent $\vdash A^\circ$
is provable, where $A^\circ$ is Girard's translation of $A$ with atoms translated by $f$.

articles.title: Separating a new hypothesis in the translation
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map propositional atoms to CLL
propositions, let $\Gamma$ be a finite set of propositional formulas, $A$ a propositional formula
and $c$ a CLL proposition. Write $B^\circ$ for Girard's translation of a formula $B$ with atoms
translated by $f$, and $?\Delta^{\circ\perp}$ for the multiset of the propositions
$?\big((B^\circ)^\perp\big)$ for $B \in \Delta$. If the CLL sequent
$\vdash c, ?(\Gamma \cup \{A\})^{\circ\perp}$ is provable, then so is
$\vdash ?\big((A^\circ)^\perp\big), c, ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$.

When $A \in \Gamma$ the conclusion follows by weakening.

articles.title: Girard's translation of an implication
articles.statement:
For every map $f$ from propositional atoms to CLL
propositions and all propositional formulas $A$ and $B$, $(A \to B)^\circ = {!A^\circ} \multimap
B^\circ$, where $C^\circ$ denotes Girard's translation of a formula $C$ with atoms translated by
$f$ and $\multimap$ is linear implication in CLL.

articles.title: Girard's translation
articles.statement:
Given a map $f$ from propositional atoms to CLL propositions, the
translation $A \mapsto A^\circ$ of propositional formulas into CLL is defined by recursion:
$a^\circ = f(a)$ for an atom $a$, $(A \wedge B)^\circ = A^\circ \mathbin{\&} B^\circ$,
$(A \vee B)^\circ = {!A^\circ} \oplus {!B^\circ}$, and $(A \to B)^\circ$ is the multiplicative
disjunction (par) of $?\big((A^\circ)^\perp\big)$ and $B^\circ$, that is, the linear implication
${!A^\circ} \multimap B^\circ$.

articles.title: Weakening by translated hypotheses
articles.statement:
Let $f$ map propositional atoms to CLL propositions.
If a CLL sequent $\vdash \Delta$ is provable, then for every multiset $\Gamma$ of propositional
formulas the sequent $\vdash ?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}, \Delta$ is provable, where $?\Gamma^{\circ\perp}$
is the multiset of the propositions $?\big((A^\circ)^\perp\big)$ for $A \in \Gamma$ and $A^\circ$
is Girard's translation of $A$ with atoms translated by $f$.

articles.title: Adjacency table of the implication graph
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the hash map that
sends each literal over the variables of $\varphi$ to the list of its implication-graph
successors, that is, of the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ with an implication edge
from it to $m$.

The table is computed once so that the SCC traversal looks successor lists up in expected
constant time.

articles.title: 2-SAT characterization
articles.statement:
**2-SAT characterization** (Aspvall, Plass, Tarjan): a 2-CNF formula is satisfiable iff
it has no empty clause and no variable `x` such that `x` and `¬x` reach each other in the
implication graph.

articles.title: Correctness of the SCC-based 2-SAT procedure
articles.statement:
For every CNF formula $\varphi$ in which
every clause has at most two literals, the SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure returns true on
$\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the procedure returns
false if $\varphi$ contains the empty clause; otherwise it returns true if and only if no block
of the strongly connected components computed for the implication graph of $\varphi$ contains a
literal together with its complementary literal.

articles.title: Clauses with at most two literals
articles.statement:
In a clause with at most two literals, any two different
members $a$ and $b$ are all of its members: every member $c$ of the clause equals $a$ or $b$.

articles.title: Resolution refutations give contradictory cycles
articles.statement:
If a CNF formula $\varphi$ does not
contain the empty clause and the empty clause is derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution, then
there is a variable $x$ such that the literals $x$ and $\neg x$ reach each other in the
implication graph of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Implication edge
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, there is an
implication edge from $l$ to $m$ when some clause of $\varphi$ contains both $\neg l$ and $m$,
either as two different literals or with $m$ as its only literal (so a unit clause $m$ gives
the edge from $\neg m$ to $m$).

articles.title: Reachability in the implication graph
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal $l$ reaches
a literal $m$ when there is a path of zero or more implication edges of $\varphi$ from $l$ to
$m$; that is, reachability is the reflexive-transitive closure of the implication edge
relation.

articles.title: Reachability in the finite implication graph
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals
$l$ and $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$, $m$ is reachable from $l$ in the implication graph
of $\varphi$, viewed as a finite directed graph on these literals, if and only if $l$ reaches $m$
by implication edges of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Implication graph as a finite directed graph
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the finite
directed graph whose vertices are the literals over the variables of $\varphi$, listed without
repetition, and whose out-neighbours of a literal $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of
$\varphi$ with an implication edge from $l$ to $m$, read from the adjacency table of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Resolution invariant of the implication graph
articles.statement:
A clause $C$ satisfies the invariant
with respect to a CNF formula $\varphi$ when for every literal $a$ of $C$ there is a literal
$b$ of $C$ such that the complementary literal $\lnot a$ reaches $b$ in the implication graph
of $\varphi$ (by a path of zero or more edges).

Every clause derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution satisfies this invariant.

articles.title: 2-CNF formulas
articles.statement:
A CNF formula is a 2-CNF formula when each of its clauses, viewed as a
list of literals, has length at most $2$ (repeated literals are counted with multiplicity).

articles.title: List of the literals of a CNF formula
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, this is the list of
all literals over the variables of $\varphi$, each appearing exactly once, arranged variable by
variable: for each variable $x$ of $\varphi$, the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is
immediately followed by the negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$.

articles.title: Literals over the variables of a formula
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal over
$\varphi$ is a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity
$b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that the variable $x$ occurs in $\varphi$.
These literals are the vertices of the implication graph of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Implication edges end over variables of the formula
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and
literals $l$ and $m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then
the variable of $m$ occurs in $\varphi$.

articles.title: A positive literal reaching its complement lies over a variable of the formula
articles.statement:
For a CNF
formula $\varphi$ and a variable $x$, if the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ reaches the
negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$, then $x$ occurs in
$\varphi$.

articles.title: Complement of a literal over a formula
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the complement of a
literal $(x, b)$ over the variables of $\varphi$ is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$, which is again a
literal over the variables of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Complement of a literal
articles.statement:
The complement of a literal $(x, b)$, with variable index
$x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $b$, is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$: same variable, opposite
polarity.

articles.title: Satisfying assignments respect implication edges
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a 2-CNF formula and
$\sigma$ an assignment of truth values to the variables that satisfies $\varphi$. If the
implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from a literal $l$ to a literal $m$ and $\sigma$
satisfies $l$, then $\sigma$ satisfies $m$.

articles.title: Skew symmetry of the implication graph
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and
$m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then it also has the
contrapositive edge from $\lnot m$ to $\lnot l$, where $\lnot$ denotes the complementary
literal.

articles.title: Successors in the implication graph
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $l$ a literal
over the variables of $\varphi$, and write $\neg l$ for the complementary literal. The
successors of $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ such that the
implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$: some clause of $\varphi$ contains
$\neg l$ and $m$, either as two different literals or as its only literal. They are listed
without repetition, in the order of the list of all literals over the variables of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Duplicate-free list of the variables of a CNF formula
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$,
this is the list of the variables occurring in the literals of $\varphi$, each exactly once,
in the order of their last occurrences when the clauses of $\varphi$ and their literals are
read from first to last.

articles.title: Congruence for the model count
articles.statement:
Let $x_1, \dots, x_k$ be a list of variables, $f$ and $g$
functions from assignments to truth values, and $\sigma$ an assignment. If $f(\tau) = g(\tau)$ for
every assignment $\tau$ such that $\tau(x) = \sigma(x)$ for every variable $x$ not in the list,
then the model counts of $f$ and of $g$ over $x_1, \dots, x_k$ from $\sigma$ are equal.

articles.title: Model count by enumeration
articles.statement:
An assignment is a map $\sigma$ from the variables, which are
natural numbers, to the truth values $\mathrm{false}$ and $\mathrm{true}$. For a list
$x_1, \dots, x_k$ of variables, a function $f$ from assignments to truth values, and an assignment
$\sigma$, the model count of $f$ over $x_1, \dots, x_k$ from $\sigma$ is the number of tuples
$(b_1, \dots, b_k) \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^k$ such that $f$ is true at the assignment
obtained from $\sigma$ by setting $x_1$ to $b_1$, then $x_2$ to $b_2$, and so on up to setting
$x_k$ to $b_k$, a later setting overriding an earlier one of the same variable.

When $x_1, \dots, x_k$ are distinct, this is the number of assignments that agree with $\sigma$
outside $x_1, \dots, x_k$ and make $f$ true.

articles.title: Correctness of the satisfy-count
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a natural number and $t$ a diagram ordered
from $0$ (tested variables strictly increase along every path) in which every tested variable is
below $m$. Then for every assignment $\sigma$, the satisfy-count of $t$ below $m$ equals the model
count of the function $\tau \mapsto t(\tau)$ over the variables $0, 1, \dots, m - 1$ from
$\sigma$, where $t(\tau)$ is the value of $t$ under $\tau$. In other words, it is the number of
assignments to the variables $0, \dots, m - 1$ that make $t$ true.

articles.title: The satisfy-count from a variable counts models
articles.statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers and
$t$ a diagram ordered from $n$ (every tested variable is at least $n$, and tested variables
strictly increase along every path) in which every tested variable is below $m$. Then for every
assignment $\sigma$, the one-pass satisfy-count $c_m(n, t)$ of $t$ from $n$ with bound $m$ equals
the model count of the function $\tau \mapsto t(\tau)$ over the variables $n, n + 1, \dots, m - 1$
from $\sigma$ (no variables when $m \le n$), where $t(\tau)$ is the value of $t$ under $\tau$.

articles.title: One-pass satisfy-count from a variable
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $m$ and $n$ and a diagram $t$,
the satisfy-count $c_m(n, t)$ of $t$ from $n$ with bound $m$ is defined by recursion on $t$: a
leaf $\mathrm{true}$ gives $2^{m - n}$, a leaf $\mathrm{false}$ gives $0$, and a node testing the
variable $v$ with child $t_0$ for false and child $t_1$ for true gives
$2^{v - n} (c_m(v + 1, t_0) + c_m(v + 1, t_1))$. Here $m - n$ and $v - n$ are truncated
subtraction, equal to $0$ when the difference would be negative.

For $t$ ordered from $n$ whose tested variables are all below $m$, $c_m(n, t)$ is the number of
assignments to the variables $n, \dots, m - 1$ that make $t$ true.

articles.title: Satisfy-count
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$ and a diagram $t$, the satisfy-count of $t$ below
$m$ is the one-pass satisfy-count $c_m(0, t)$ of $t$ from the variable $0$ with bound $m$.

When $t$ is ordered from $0$ and every variable it tests is below $m$, this is the number of
assignments to the variables $0, \dots, m - 1$ that make $t$ true.

articles.title: Variables below a bound
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$, a diagram has its variables below $m$
when every variable tested at a node of the diagram is less than $m$.

articles.title: Bryant's apply operation
articles.statement:
For a binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$ and binary decision
diagrams $t_1, t_2$, the diagram $A_{\mathrm{op}}(t_1, t_2)$ is defined by recursion. If $t_1$
and $t_2$ are leaves with values $a$ and $b$, it is the leaf with value $\mathrm{op}(a, b)$.
Otherwise let $v$ be the smallest variable tested at the root of $t_1$ or of $t_2$ (a leaf tests
none), and for $i = 1, 2$ let $\ell_i$ and $h_i$ be the low and high children of $t_i$ if its
root tests $v$, and $\ell_i = h_i = t_i$ otherwise. The result is
$\mathrm{mk}(v, A_{\mathrm{op}}(\ell_1, \ell_2), A_{\mathrm{op}}(h_1, h_2))$, where
$\mathrm{mk}(v, \ell, h)$ is $\ell$ if $\ell = h$, and otherwise the node testing $v$ with low
child $\ell$ and high child $h$.

articles.title: Binary decision diagram
articles.statement:
A binary decision diagram, in tree form, is either a leaf
carrying a Boolean value, or a node consisting of a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and two
diagrams: the low child, for $v$ false, and the high child, for $v$ true.

articles.title: Reduced ordered diagrams are equal iff they have the same values
articles.statement:
If $t_1$ and $t_2$ are
reduced ordered binary decision diagrams, then $t_1 = t_2$ if and only if $t_1$ and $t_2$ have
the same value under every assignment of Boolean values to the variables.

articles.title: Unsatisfiable reduced ordered diagrams
articles.statement:
A reduced ordered binary decision diagram $t$ is
the leaf with value false if and only if $t$ has value false under every assignment of Boolean
values to the variables.

articles.title: Canonicity
articles.statement:
**Canonicity** (Bryant): two reduced ordered diagrams with the same function are
equal.

articles.title: Apply computes the operation pointwise
articles.statement:
For every binary Boolean operation
$\mathrm{op}$, all binary decision diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, and every assignment $\sigma$ of
Boolean values to the variables, the value under $\sigma$ of the diagram
$\mathrm{apply}(\mathrm{op}, t_1, t_2)$ obtained from $t_1$ and $t_2$ by Bryant's apply operation
under $\mathrm{op}$ is $\mathrm{op}(a_1, a_2)$, where $a_i$ is the value of $t_i$ under $\sigma$.

articles.title: Fixing the top variable of an ordered node
articles.statement:
Let $t$ be a node testing the variable $v$
with low child $\ell$ and high child $h$, and suppose $t$ is ordered from some $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value
of $t$ under $\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) is the value of
$h$ under $\sigma$ if $b$ is true, and the value of $\ell$ under $\sigma$ if $b$ is false.

articles.title: Independence from variables below the order
articles.statement:
Let $t$ be a binary decision diagram
ordered from $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $v < n$ be a variable. For every assignment $\sigma$ of
Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value of $t$ under
$\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) equals the value of $t$ under
$\sigma$.

articles.title: Evaluation of a binary decision diagram
articles.statement:
Under an assignment $\sigma$ of a Boolean value
to each variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$, the value of a leaf is its Boolean value, and the value of a
node testing $v$ is the value of its high child if $\sigma(v)$ is true and the value of its low
child if $\sigma(v)$ is false.

articles.title: Reduced ordered binary decision diagram
articles.statement:
A binary decision diagram is a reduced ordered
binary decision diagram (ROBDD), for the natural order on variables, when it is ordered from
$0$ (the tested variables strictly increase along every path) and reduced (no node has two
equal children).

articles.title: Node constructor removing a redundant test
articles.statement:
For a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and diagrams
$\ell$ and $h$, the diagram $\mathrm{mk}(v, \ell, h)$ is $\ell$ if $\ell = h$, and otherwise the
node that tests $v$ with $\ell$ as its false-child and $h$ as its true-child.

articles.title: Equal BDDs iff equal truth tables
articles.statement:
For propositions $A$ and $B$ over natural-number
atoms, the binary decision diagrams of $A$ and $B$ are equal if and only if $A$ and $B$ have the
same truth value under every valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$.

Comparing the diagrams therefore decides truth-table equivalence.

articles.title: Satisfiable iff the BDD is not the false leaf
articles.statement:
For a proposition $A$ over
natural-number atoms, the binary decision diagram of $A$ is not the leaf false if and only if
some valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ makes $A$ true.

Both sides always hold: the valuation that makes every atom true satisfies every proposition
built from atoms by conjunction, disjunction and implication.

articles.title: Diagram of a proposition
articles.statement:
Each proposition $A$ whose atoms are natural numbers is sent
to a binary decision diagram by recursion on $A$: an atom $x$ goes to the node testing $x$ with
the leaf false as its false-child and the leaf true as its true-child, and a conjunction
$A \wedge B$, disjunction $A \vee B$ or implication $A \to B$ goes to the result of apply on the
diagrams of $A$ and $B$ under the Boolean operation and, or, or $(a, b) \mapsto \lnot a \lor b$
respectively.

articles.title: Apply preserves orderedness
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{op}$ be a binary Boolean operation and $n$ a
natural number. If the diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$ are both ordered from $n$, then the result of
apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is ordered from $n$.

articles.title: Diagrams ordered from a variable
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, a diagram is ordered from
$n$ when every variable it tests is at least $n$ and the tested variables strictly increase
along every path. Recursively: every leaf is ordered from $n$, and the node testing $v$ with
children $\ell$ and $h$ is ordered from $n$ when $n \le v$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are ordered
from $v + 1$.

articles.title: Apply returns reduced diagrams
articles.statement:
For every binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$ and all
diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, the result of apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is reduced.

articles.title: Reduced diagrams
articles.statement:
A diagram is reduced when no node in it has two equal children: every
leaf is reduced, and the node testing $v$ with children $\ell$ and $h$ is reduced when
$\ell \ne h$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are reduced.

articles.title: Binary decision diagrams have positive size
articles.statement:
For every binary decision diagram $t$,
the size of $t$ (its number of leaves and nodes, counted in tree form) is strictly positive.

articles.title: Size of a diagram
articles.statement:
The size of a diagram is its number of leaves and nodes, counted in
tree form: a leaf has size $1$, and a node with children $\ell$ and $h$ has size one more than the
sum of the sizes of $\ell$ and $h$.

articles.title: The all-true valuation satisfies every proposition
articles.statement:
Every proposition $A$ over atoms
indexed by natural numbers, built from atoms with $\land$, $\lor$ and $\to$ only, evaluates to
true under the valuation that makes every atom true.

articles.title: The path assignment satisfies an ordered diagram
articles.statement:
Let $t$ be a binary decision diagram
ordered from some $n$ (every tested variable is at least $n$, and tested variables strictly
increase along every path). If the satisfying-path search on $t$ returns a path $p$, then $t$
evaluates to true under the assignment read off $p$.

articles.title: Satisfiability with one variable fixed to false
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a proposition over atoms
indexed by natural numbers, let $t$ be its ROBDD, and let $f$ be a natural number. Then $A$
evaluates to true under some valuation $\sigma$ with $\sigma(f) = \mathrm{false}$ if and only
if the cofactor $t[f := \mathrm{false}]$ is not the leaf $\mathrm{false}$.

The variable $f$ can, for instance, play the role of falsum. Without such a constraint, every
proposition over atoms indexed by natural numbers is satisfied by the all-true valuation.

articles.title: Existential quantification of a diagram
articles.statement:
For a variable $x$ and a binary decision diagram
$t$, the existential quantification of $t$ over $x$ is the diagram obtained by combining the
cofactors $t[x := \mathrm{false}]$ and $t[x := \mathrm{true}]$ with Bryant's apply under
disjunction.

articles.title: Universal quantification of a diagram
articles.statement:
For a variable $x$ and a binary decision diagram
$t$, the universal quantification of $t$ over $x$ is the diagram obtained by combining the
cofactors $t[x := \mathrm{false}]$ and $t[x := \mathrm{true}]$ with Bryant's apply under
conjunction.

articles.title: Existential quantification yields an ROBDD
articles.statement:
If $t$ is an ordered binary decision diagram
(tested variables strictly increase along every path), then for every variable $x$ the
existential quantification of $t$ over $x$ is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram.

articles.title: Restriction yields an ROBDD
articles.statement:
If $t$ is an ordered binary decision diagram (tested
variables strictly increase along every path), then for every variable $x$ and every Boolean
$b$ the cofactor $t[x := b]$ is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram.

articles.title: Assignment read off a path
articles.statement:
For a path $p$, given as a list of pairs $(v, b)$ of a
variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $b$, the assignment read off $p$ sends a variable $x$
to the Boolean of the first pair in $p$ whose variable is $x$, and to $\mathrm{false}$ if $x$
occurs in no pair of $p$.

articles.title: Satisfy-one for propositions
articles.statement:
For every proposition $A$ over atoms indexed by natural
numbers, the satisfying-path search on the ROBDD of $A$ returns a path $p$, and $A$ evaluates to
true under the assignment read off $p$.

Every such proposition is satisfiable, by the all-true valuation; the path usually gives a
different model.

articles.title: Restriction yields a reduced diagram
articles.statement:
For every binary decision diagram $t$, every
variable $x$ and every Boolean $b$, the cofactor $t[x := b]$ is reduced: no node has two equal
children.

Nodes that restriction keeps are rebuilt with the node constructor that removes redundant
tests, so the input need not be reduced.

articles.title: Restriction of a binary decision diagram
articles.statement:
For a variable $x$ and a Boolean $b$, the
restriction (cofactor) $t[x := b]$ of a binary decision diagram $t$ is defined recursively: a
leaf is kept; a node testing $x$ is replaced by the restriction of its $\mathrm{hi}$ child if $b$
is true and of its $\mathrm{lo}$ child if $b$ is false; and a node testing any other variable
$v$ is rebuilt from the restrictions of its two children with the reducing node constructor,
which returns the common child when the two are equal and a node testing $v$ otherwise.

articles.title: Reduced diagrams other than false have a satisfying path
articles.statement:
If a binary decision diagram
$t$ is reduced and is not the leaf $\mathrm{false}$, then the search for a satisfying path in $t$
succeeds: it returns a path from the root of $t$ to a leaf $\mathrm{true}$.

articles.title: Satisfy-one with a variable fixed to false
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a proposition over
natural-number atoms and let $f$ be a natural number. If some assignment $\sigma$ with
$\sigma(f) = \mathrm{false}$ satisfies $A$, then the search for a satisfying path in the
restriction at $f := \mathrm{false}$ of the ROBDD of $A$ returns a path $p$, and the assignment
read off $p$ (the recorded value on each variable of $p$, false elsewhere), changed to send $f$
to $\mathrm{false}$, satisfies $A$.

articles.title: Satisfying path of a binary decision diagram
articles.statement:
The satisfying path of a diagram is found
by a depth-first search for a leaf $\mathrm{true}$ that tries the $\mathrm{hi}$ (true) child of
each node before its $\mathrm{lo}$ (false) child. It is returned as the list of pairs $(v, c)$ of
the variables $v$ tested along the path with the branches $c$ taken (empty at a leaf
$\mathrm{true}$), and the search returns nothing when the diagram has no leaf $\mathrm{true}$.

articles.title: Restriction reduces the number of variables
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let
$\ell = (x, b)$ be a literal whose variable $x$ occurs in $F$. Then the restriction of $F$
by $\ell$ has strictly fewer distinct variables than $F$.

articles.title: Accumulating CNF builder
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal
$(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and
false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF
$\mathcal{A}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the disjoining
builder $\mathcal{O}_p$. For an atom $a$, $\mathcal{A}_p(a, S)$ is the unit clause
$[(\iota(a), p)]$ followed by the clauses of $S$. Conjunction-like nodes thread the accumulator:
$\mathcal{A}_1(A \land B, S) = \mathcal{A}_1(A, \mathcal{A}_1(B, S))$,
$\mathcal{A}_0(A \lor B, S) = \mathcal{A}_0(A, \mathcal{A}_0(B, S))$ and
$\mathcal{A}_0(A \to B, S) = \mathcal{A}_1(A, \mathcal{A}_0(B, S))$. Disjunction-like nodes go
through $\mathcal{O}$: writing $X \mathbin{+\!\!+} S$ for the clauses of $X$ followed by those of
$S$ and $[\,]$ for the empty CNF,
$\mathcal{A}_1(A \lor B, S) = \mathcal{O}_1(A, \mathcal{A}_1(B, [\,])) \mathbin{+\!\!+} S$,
$\mathcal{A}_1(A \to B, S) = \mathcal{O}_0(A, \mathcal{A}_1(B, [\,])) \mathbin{+\!\!+} S$ and
$\mathcal{A}_0(A \land B, S) = \mathcal{O}_0(A, \mathcal{A}_0(B, [\,])) \mathbin{+\!\!+} S$.

An assignment $\sigma$ satisfies $\mathcal{A}_p(\varphi, S)$ exactly when $\varphi$ has truth
value $p$ under $\sigma \circ \iota$ and $\sigma$ satisfies $S$.

articles.title: CNF of a proposition at a polarity
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For a
polarity $p$ and a proposition $\varphi$, the CNF of $\varphi$ at polarity $p$ is the result of the
accumulating CNF builder at polarity $p$ on $\varphi$ with the empty CNF as accumulator; the atom
$a$ becomes the variable $\iota(a)$.

An assignment $\sigma$ satisfies it exactly when $\varphi$ has truth value $p$ under
$\sigma \circ \iota$, so it is a CNF of $\varphi$ when $p$ is true and of the Boolean complement of
$\varphi$ when $p$ is false. Only the requested polarity is built: a proposition already in
conjunctive normal form gets a CNF of linear size at polarity true, although the CNF of its
complement can be exponentially larger.

articles.title: Disjoining CNF builder
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal
$(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and
false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF
$\mathcal{O}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the accumulating
CNF builder $\mathcal{A}_p$. Write $X \otimes S$ for the disjunction of two CNFs $X$ and $S$ and
$[\,]$ for the empty CNF. For an atom $a$, $\mathcal{O}_p(a, S) = U \otimes S$, where $U$ is the
CNF whose only clause is the unit clause $[(\iota(a), p)]$. Disjunction-like nodes are consumed
from the left: $\mathcal{O}_1(A \lor B, S) = \mathcal{O}_1(A, \mathcal{O}_1(B, S))$,
$\mathcal{O}_1(A \to B, S) = \mathcal{O}_0(A, \mathcal{O}_1(B, S))$ and
$\mathcal{O}_0(A \land B, S) = \mathcal{O}_0(A, \mathcal{O}_0(B, S))$. Conjunction-like nodes go
through $\mathcal{A}$:
$\mathcal{O}_1(A \land B, S) = \mathcal{A}_1(A, \mathcal{A}_1(B, [\,])) \otimes S$,
$\mathcal{O}_0(A \lor B, S) = \mathcal{A}_0(A, \mathcal{A}_0(B, [\,])) \otimes S$ and
$\mathcal{O}_0(A \to B, S) = \mathcal{A}_1(A, \mathcal{A}_0(B, [\,])) \otimes S$.

An assignment $\sigma$ satisfies $\mathcal{O}_p(\varphi, S)$ exactly when $\varphi$ has truth
value $p$ under $\sigma \circ \iota$ or $\sigma$ satisfies $S$.

articles.title: Satisfiability means having a satisfying assignment
articles.statement:
A CNF formula $\varphi$ is
satisfiable if and only if there is an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true},
\mathrm{false}\}$ that satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: Satisfiability of a CNF with falsum false
articles.statement:
Let the atoms have a distinguished atom $\bot$
and let $\iota$ be an injective numbering of the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition
$A$, the CNF consisting of the unit clause with the single negative literal on variable
$\iota(\bot)$ followed by the clauses of the CNF of $A$ (atom $a$ read as variable $\iota(a)$) is
satisfiable if and only if some valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot)$ false makes $A$ true.

articles.title: CNF formula
articles.statement:
A CNF formula is a finite list of CNF clauses, read as the conjunction of its
clauses.

articles.title: CNF clause
articles.statement:
A CNF clause is a finite list of literals, each a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable
index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$.

articles.title: Satisfiability of a CNF formula
articles.statement:
A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable when there is an
assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that every clause $C$ of
$\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.

articles.title: Disjunction of two CNFs
articles.statement:
For CNFs $\varphi = C_1 \land \dots \land C_m$ and
$\psi = D_1 \land \dots \land D_n$, their disjunction is the CNF with one clause $C_i \lor D_j$
(the literals of $C_i$ followed by those of $D_j$) for each pair $(i, j)$, listed with $i$ as the
outer and $j$ as the inner index. It expresses $(\bigwedge_i C_i) \lor (\bigwedge_j D_j)$ as
$\bigwedge_{i,j} (C_i \lor D_j)$.

articles.title: The restricted variable no longer occurs
articles.statement:
For every CNF formula $F$ and every literal
$\ell = (x, b)$, the variable $x$ does not occur in the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$.

articles.title: Restriction of a CNF formula by a literal
articles.statement:
Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the
restriction of a CNF formula $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is obtained by deleting every clause of $\varphi$
that contains $\ell$ and replacing every other clause by its restriction by $\ell$, the clause
obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of either polarity; the remaining
clauses keep their order.

The deleted clauses are true under every assignment that gives $x$ the value $b$.

articles.title: Restriction of a clause by a literal
articles.statement:
Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the restriction
of a clause by $\ell$ is the clause obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of
either polarity, keeping the other literals in order.

articles.title: Unit propagation preserves satisfiability
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a CNF formula that contains the
unit clause whose only literal is $\ell$. Then $F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction
of $F$ by $\ell$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: Splitting on a variable
articles.statement:
For every CNF formula $F$ and every variable $x$, the formula
$F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is
satisfiable or the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: Satisfaction of a clause
articles.statement:
An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true},
\mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF clause $C$ when at least one literal of $C$ is satisfied by $v$,
that is, $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.

articles.title: Satisfaction of a CNF formula
articles.statement:
An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true},
\mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF formula $\varphi$ when $v$ satisfies every clause of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Satisfaction depends only on the occurring variables
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let
$v_1, v_2$ be assignments of Booleans to variables with $v_1(x) = v_2(x)$ for every variable $x$
occurring in $F$. If $v_1$ satisfies $F$, then $v_2$ satisfies $F$.

articles.title: Lifting a satisfying assignment from a restriction
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a CNF formula,
$\ell = (x, b)$ a literal and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables. If $v$ satisfies the
restriction of $F$ by $\ell$, then the assignment that agrees with $v$ except that it sends $x$
to $b$ satisfies $F$.

articles.title: Satisfaction of a restricted CNF formula
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $\ell = (x, b)$
a literal, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$ satisfies the
restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: Satisfaction of a restricted clause
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a clause, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal that
does not occur in $C$, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$
satisfies the restriction of $C$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $C$.

articles.title: Equivalent CNF
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition $A$
and every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables, the CNF of $A$
built with atom $a$ as variable $\iota(a)$ is satisfied by $\sigma$ if and only if $A$ evaluates
to true under the valuation $\sigma \circ \iota$ of the atoms.

articles.title: Satisfaction of a literal
articles.statement:
An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true},
\mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a literal $(x, b)$, with variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity
$b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, when $v(x) = b$.

articles.title: CNF of a proposition
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. The CNF of a
proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity true, with the atom $a$ as the variable $\iota(a)$.

An assignment $\sigma$ satisfies it exactly when $A$ is true under $\sigma \circ \iota$.

articles.title: CNF of the complement of a proposition
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers.
The complement CNF of a proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity false, with the atom $a$ as the
variable $\iota(a)$.

An assignment $\sigma$ satisfies it exactly when $A$ is false under $\sigma \circ \iota$. This is
not the negation $\lnot A$, which is $A \to \bot$ with $\bot$ an atom: that proposition can be
true together with $A$ when the atom $\bot$ is true.

articles.title: Variables of a CNF formula
articles.statement:
The variables of a CNF formula $\varphi$ form the union of the
sets of variables of its clauses, that is, the finite set of natural numbers $x$ such that some
clause of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.

articles.title: Restricting by an occurring variable shrinks the variable set
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF
formula and $(x, b)$ a literal. If $x$ is a variable of $\varphi$, then the set of variables of
the restriction of $\varphi$ by $(x, b)$ is a proper subset of the set of variables of
$\varphi$.

articles.title: Restriction does not add variables
articles.statement:
For every CNF formula $\varphi$ and every literal
$\ell$, every variable of the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is a variable of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Variables of a clause
articles.statement:
The variables of a CNF clause $C$ form the finite set of natural
numbers $x$ such that $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.

articles.title: Atoms of a proposition
articles.statement:
The atoms of a proposition $A$ form the finite set of atoms
occurring in $A$: an atom $x$ has the single atom $x$, and the atoms of $B \wedge C$,
$B \vee C$ and $B \to C$ are the atoms of $B$ together with the atoms of $C$.

articles.title: Boolean quantification over an atom
articles.statement:
For an atom $p$ and a proposition $A$, the Boolean
quantification $\exists p.\, A$ is the disjunction $A[p := \top] \vee A[p := \bot]$, where
$A[p := \top]$ and $A[p := \bot]$ replace the atom $p$ in $A$ by the constant
$\top = (\bot \to \bot)$ and by $\bot$ respectively.

articles.title: Boolean quantification over a list of atoms
articles.statement:
For a list of atoms $p_1, \dots, p_n$ and a
proposition $A$, the iterated Boolean quantification $\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is
$\exists p_1.\, \exists p_2.\, \cdots \exists p_n.\, A$: $A$ is quantified over $p_n$ first and over
$p_1$ last, and for the empty list the result is $A$ itself.

articles.title: The truth value depends only on the atoms
articles.statement:
If two Boolean valuations $v$ and $w$ agree on
every atom of a proposition $A$, then $A$ has the same truth-table value under $v$ as under
$w$.

articles.title: Truth of a Boolean quantification over a list of atoms
articles.statement:
Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be a list
of atoms that does not contain $\bot$, let $A$ be a proposition and let $v$ be a Boolean
valuation with $v(\bot)$ false. Then the iterated Boolean quantification
$\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is true under $v$ if and only if $A$ is true under some valuation
$w$ that agrees with $v$ on every atom not in the list.

articles.title: Craig interpolation for classical natural deduction
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such
that $A \to B$ is derivable without assumptions in classical propositional logic $\mathrm{CPL}$
(natural deduction with the axioms $\neg\neg C \to C$). Then there is a proposition $I$ whose
atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$, such that $A \to I$
and $I \to B$ are both derivable without assumptions in $\mathrm{CPL}$.

articles.title: Craig interpolation, semantic form
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such that every
Boolean valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true also makes $B$ true. Then there is
a proposition $I$ whose atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$,
such that every valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true makes $I$ true, and every
valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $I$ true makes $B$ true.

articles.title: Substituting a truth value for an atom
articles.statement:
For an atom $p$, a Boolean $b$ and a proposition
$A$, the proposition $A[p := b]$ is obtained from $A$ by replacing every occurrence of the atom
$p$ by the constant $\top$, written $\bot \to \bot$, if $b$ is true, and by $\bot$ if $b$ is
false.

articles.title: Davis-Putnam elimination preserves satisfiability
articles.statement:
For every variable $x$ and every CNF
formula $\varphi$, the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$ is satisfiable if and
only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: Correctness of the Davis-Putnam procedure
articles.statement:
For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the
Davis-Putnam procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: The Davis-Putnam procedure
articles.statement:
Given a CNF formula $\varphi$, eliminate the variables
that occur in $\varphi$ one after another, each exactly once, in the order of their first
occurrence in $\varphi$, each elimination being applied to the result of the previous one. The
procedure returns true if the resulting formula does not contain the empty clause, and false if
it does.

articles.title: Successive elimination of a list of variables
articles.statement:
Given a list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of variables
and a CNF formula $\varphi$, eliminate $x_1$ from $\varphi$, then $x_2$ from the result, and so on
up to $x_n$. For the empty list the result is $\varphi$.

articles.title: Davis-Putnam elimination of a variable
articles.statement:
Eliminating a variable $x$ from a CNF formula
$\varphi$ gives the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$ that contain neither $x$ nor
$\neg x$, followed by the resolvents on $x$ of $C$ and $D$, for every clause $C$ of $\varphi$ that
contains $x$ but not $\neg x$ and every clause $D$ of $\varphi$ that contains $\neg x$ but not $x$.
Clauses containing both $x$ and $\neg x$ are dropped.

articles.title: Completeness of a Davis-Putnam step
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be a variable, $\varphi$ a CNF formula and
$\sigma$ an assignment that satisfies the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$. Then
there is a truth value $b$ such that the assignment that agrees with $\sigma$ except that it sends
$x$ to $b$ satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: Resolvents do not mention the resolved variable
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be a variable and let $C$ and $D$
be clauses such that $C$ does not contain $\neg x$ and $D$ does not contain $x$. Then no literal
of the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$ has variable $x$.

In particular, the resolvents added when eliminating $x$ do not mention $x$.

articles.title: Clauses containing a variable only negatively
articles.statement:
For a variable $x$ and a CNF formula
$\varphi$, the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$, in their order, that contain the
literal $\neg x$ and do not contain the literal $x$.

articles.title: Clauses containing a variable only positively
articles.statement:
For a variable $x$ and a CNF formula
$\varphi$, the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$, in their order, that contain the
literal $x$ and do not contain the literal $\neg x$.

articles.title: Soundness of a Davis-Putnam step
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be a variable and $\varphi$ a CNF formula. Every
assignment that satisfies $\varphi$ also satisfies the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by
eliminating $x$.

articles.title: Variable list for Davis–Putnam elimination
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the list of the
variables occurring in the literals of $\varphi$, each listed exactly once, in order of first
occurrence when the clauses of $\varphi$, and the literals within each clause, are read from left
to right.

Removing the repetitions takes time quadratic in the number of literal occurrences, which the
eliminations dominate.

articles.title: Boolean clause satisfaction check
articles.statement:
For an assignment $v$ of Boolean values to the
variables $0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and a clause $C$, whose literals are pairs $(x, b)$ of a variable
$x$ and a polarity $b$, this Boolean is true exactly when some literal $(x, b)$ of $C$ satisfies
$v(x) = b$.

articles.title: DPLL with a fuel budget
articles.statement:
Given a natural number $n$ (the fuel) and a CNF formula
$\varphi$, the procedure returns a Boolean value. Literals are pairs $(x, b)$ of a variable $x$
and a polarity $b$. With fuel $0$ the procedure returns true exactly when $\varphi$ has no
clauses. With fuel $n + 1$ it returns true if $\varphi$ has no clauses, and otherwise returns
false if some clause of $\varphi$ is empty. Otherwise, if some clause of $\varphi$ consists of
a single literal, it takes the first such literal $\ell$ in source order and returns the result
of the procedure with fuel $n$ on the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$. Otherwise, if some
variable occurs in $\varphi$, it takes the first such variable $x$ in source order and returns
true exactly when the procedure with fuel $n$ returns true on the restriction of $\varphi$ by
$(x, \mathrm{true})$ or on the restriction of $\varphi$ by $(x, \mathrm{false})$; if no variable
occurs, it returns false.

The restriction of $\varphi$ by a literal $(x, b)$ deletes every clause containing $(x, b)$ and
removes every literal with variable $x$ from the remaining clauses. A decision branches on both
polarities, a unit literal gives a single recursive call, and no satisfying assignment is
returned.

articles.title: The DPLL procedure
articles.statement:
On a CNF formula $\varphi$, the DPLL procedure runs DPLL with fuel
equal to the number of distinct variables occurring in $\varphi$ and returns its Boolean result.

articles.title: First unit literal
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses, this returns
the literal $\ell$ of the first clause of $\varphi$ that consists of the single literal $\ell$,
and returns nothing when no clause of $\varphi$ has exactly one literal.

articles.title: First variable of a CNF formula
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses,
this returns the variable of the first literal of the first nonempty clause of $\varphi$, that
is, the first variable occurring in $\varphi$ in source order, and returns nothing when every
clause of $\varphi$ is empty (in particular when $\varphi$ has no clauses).

articles.title: Boolean formula satisfaction check
articles.statement:
For an assignment $v$ of Boolean values to the
variables $0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, this Boolean is true exactly when every
clause of $\varphi$ passes the Boolean clause satisfaction check for $v$, that is, every clause
contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.

articles.title: Correctness of DPLL with sufficient fuel
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $n$ be a
natural number at least the number of distinct variables occurring in $\varphi$. Then DPLL with
fuel $n$ returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: Correctness of DPLL
articles.statement:
For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the DPLL procedure returns true on
$\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves and reflects classical derivability
articles.statement:
For every proposition $A$, let $A^*$ be its translation into $\to$ and $\bot$, which keeps atoms
and implications and recursively replaces each $B \wedge C$ by $(B \to (C \to \bot)) \to \bot$
and each $B \vee C$ by $(B \to \bot) \to C$. Then $A^*$ is derivable from no hypotheses in
classical propositional logic if and only if $A$ is.

articles.title: Correctness of the Shannon expansion
articles.statement:
Let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be a list of atoms and let
$f$ assign a truth value to every valuation of the atoms, such that $f(v) = f(w)$ whenever $v$
and $w$ agree on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. Then for every valuation $v$ that makes $\bot$ false, the
Shannon expansion of $f$ over $x_1, \dots, x_n$ has truth value $f(v)$ under $v$.

articles.title: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves truth values
articles.statement:
For every proposition $A$
and every valuation $v$ that makes $\bot$ false, the translation of $A$ into $\to$ and $\bot$
has the same truth value under $v$ as $A$.

articles.title: Functional completeness
articles.statement:
Every Boolean function of the atoms in a finite list is the
truth table, on valuations with `⊥` false, of some proposition.

articles.title: Functional completeness of `→` and `⊥`
articles.statement:
Every Boolean function of the atoms in a
finite list is the truth table, on valuations with `⊥` false, of a proposition built with
`→` alone.

articles.title: Propositions built from $\to$ and $\bot$
articles.statement:
A proposition is built from $\to$ and $\bot$
when it contains no conjunction and no disjunction: every atom (including $\bot$, which is an
atom) is, and $A \to B$ is exactly when both $A$ and $B$ are.

articles.title: Shannon expansion
articles.statement:
Let $f$ assign a truth value to every valuation of the atoms. The
Shannon expansion $S(\ell, f)$ of $f$ over a list $\ell$ of atoms is defined by recursion on
$\ell$. For the empty list it is $\bot \to \bot$ if $f$ is true at the valuation that makes every
atom false, and $\bot$ otherwise. For the list $x \cdot \ell$ with head $x$ and tail $\ell$,

$$
S(x \cdot \ell, f) = (x \wedge S(\ell, f_1)) \vee (\neg x \wedge S(\ell, f_0)),
$$

where $\neg x$ is $x \to \bot$, and $f_1(v) = f(v[x \mapsto \mathrm{true}])$ and
$f_0(v) = f(v[x \mapsto \mathrm{false}])$, with $v[x \mapsto b]$ the valuation $v$ changed at $x$
to $b$.

articles.title: Translation into $\to$ and $\bot$
articles.statement:
The translation $A^*$ of a proposition $A$ is defined
by recursion on $A$: each atom is unchanged, $(A \to B)^* = A^* \to B^*$,
$(A \wedge B)^* = (A^* \to (B^* \to \bot)) \to \bot$ and $(A \vee B)^* = (A^* \to \bot) \to B^*$.

articles.title: Body of a clause contained in a set
articles.statement:
For a finite set $T$ of variables and a CNF
clause $C$, this Boolean test is true exactly when every negative literal of $C$ has its
variable in $T$.

articles.title: Forward-chaining closure
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of
variables, the closure of $T$ is computed by iterating the forward-chaining step of $\varphi$:
if every variable derived from $T$ already lies in $T$, the closure is $T$; otherwise it is the
closure of the union of $T$ with the derived variables.

The iteration terminates because each step that does not stop adds a variable of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Forward-chaining step
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of variables,
the derived set consists of the variables $x$ such that some clause of $\varphi$ contains the
positive literal $x$ and has every one of its negative literals on a variable in $T$.

articles.title: Correctness of the Horn satisfiability test
articles.statement:
If $\varphi$ is a Horn CNF formula, then
the Horn satisfiability test returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

articles.title: Horn satisfiability test
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the Horn satisfiability test
returns the Boolean truth value of $\varphi$ under its least model candidate.

articles.title: Horn formula
articles.statement:
A CNF formula is a Horn formula when every clause contains at most one
distinct positive literal.

articles.title: On Horn formulas, the least model candidate lies below every model
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a
Horn CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment satisfying $\varphi$. Every variable that the least
model candidate of $\varphi$ makes true is also true under $\sigma$.

articles.title: Least model candidate
articles.statement:
For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the least model candidate is the
assignment that makes a variable true exactly when it lies in the forward-chaining closure of
the empty set under $\varphi$.

articles.title: Horn satisfiability via the least model
articles.statement:
A Horn CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if
and only if its least model candidate satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: Compaction preserves clause-length bounds
articles.statement: Compaction preserves every upper bound on clause length.

articles.title: Counting satisfying assignments over a larger variable range
articles.statement:
If every occurring name is below `N`, the count over all `Fin N` assignments is the support
count times one Boolean choice for each unused ambient variable.

articles.title: Compaction preserves clause lengths
articles.statement: Compaction preserves every clause length, in the original clause order.

articles.title: Exact variable compaction of a CNF formula
articles.statement: Rename every occurring variable by its position in the last-occurrence list.

articles.title: Unique satisfying extension in the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction
articles.statement:
Every satisfying assignment of the original formula has exactly one satisfying extension that
can differ only on the allocated fresh-variable interval.

articles.title: The parsimonious reduction outputs a duplicate-free 3-CNF
articles.statement: Every output clause has length at most three, and duplicate clauses have been removed.

articles.title: Compaction preserves the number of clauses
articles.statement: Compaction preserves the number of clauses.

articles.title: Variable compaction preserves the model count
articles.statement: Exact variable compaction preserves the number of assignments to the occurring variables.

articles.title: The parsimonious 3-CNF reduction preserves the model count
articles.statement:
The parsimonious reduction preserves the number of assignments to the variables occurring in
the formula.

articles.title: Model count of a CNF formula
articles.statement: The number of Boolean assignments to the variables occurring in a formula that satisfy it.

articles.title: Compaction preserves absence of duplicate clauses
articles.statement: Compaction preserves the absence of duplicate clauses.

articles.title: Number of fresh variables in the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction
articles.statement: The number of fresh variables used by the parsimonious width-three reduction.

articles.title: Satisfaction is preserved by variable compaction
articles.statement:
Satisfaction after compaction is satisfaction before compaction with names translated by
their exact last-occurrence positions.

articles.title: Soundness of the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction
articles.statement:
Satisfaction of the reduced formula implies satisfaction of the original formula under the
same values of the original variable names.

articles.title: Size bounds for the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction
articles.statement:
A width bound on the input gives the source bounds on allocated fresh variables and output
clauses.

articles.title: Parsimonious reduction of CNF to 3-CNF
articles.statement:
Reduce a CNF to clauses of length at most three, allocating fresh variables consecutively
from `start`. Repeated output clauses are removed in last-occurrence order.

articles.title: Variables of a compacted formula form an initial range
articles.statement: The variables of a compacted formula are exactly its dense initial range.

articles.title: Truth-table consequence
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory (a set of propositions), $\Gamma$ a context
(a finite set of propositions) and $A$ a proposition. Then $A$ is a truth-table consequence of
$\Gamma$ in $T$ when every Boolean valuation of the atoms under which all members of $T$ and all
members of $\Gamma$ evaluate to true also makes $A$ evaluate to true.

articles.title: Model existence for propositional natural deduction
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be an intuitionistic theory,
that is, one that derives $\bot \to B$ for every proposition $B$. If a set $S$ of propositions is
consistent relative to $T$, then $T \cup S$ is satisfiable: some Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms
with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ makes every member of $T$ and every member of $S$ true.

articles.title: Compactness
articles.statement:
A set of propositions is satisfiable, with `⊥` false, iff each of its
finite subsets is.

articles.title: Satisfiable sets of propositions
articles.statement:
A set $S$ of propositions is satisfiable when some
Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ makes every member of $S$
true.

articles.title: Truth-table soundness of derivability
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory, $\Gamma$ a context and $A$ a
proposition. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in natural deduction with axioms from
$T$, then $A$ is a truth-table consequence of $\Gamma$ in $T$: every Boolean valuation of the
atoms that makes all members of $T$ and of $\Gamma$ true makes $A$ true.

articles.title: Soundness of natural deduction for truth tables
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory, $\Gamma$ a context and
$A$ a proposition. For every natural-deduction derivation of $\Gamma \vdash A$ with axioms from $T$,
every Boolean valuation of the atoms that makes all members of $T$ and of $\Gamma$ true makes $A$
true.

articles.title: Consistency relative to a theory
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory, that is, a set of propositions. A
set $S$ of propositions is consistent relative to $T$ when there is no finite set
$\Gamma \subseteq S$ such that the sequent $\Gamma \vdash \bot$ is derivable in natural deduction
from $T$.

articles.title: Completeness for truth tables
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite set of propositions and $A$ a
proposition. The sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in classical propositional logic (natural
deduction with every instance of $\neg\neg B \to B$ as an axiom, where $\neg B$ abbreviates
$B \to \bot$) iff every Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ that
makes every member of $\Gamma$ true also makes $A$ true.

articles.title: Soundness and completeness for classical theories
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a classical theory, that is,
one that derives $\neg\neg B \to B$ for every proposition $B$, where $\neg B$ abbreviates
$B \to \bot$. For every finite set $\Gamma$ of propositions and every proposition $A$, the sequent
$\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable from $T$ iff every Boolean valuation of the atoms that makes every
member of $T$ and every member of $\Gamma$ true also makes $A$ true.

Here $\bot$ is a distinguished atom, and these valuations may make it true or false.

articles.title: Soundness and completeness for classical theories, with ⊥ false
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a classical
theory, that is, one that derives $\neg\neg B \to B$ for every proposition $B$, where $\neg B$
abbreviates $B \to \bot$. For every finite set $\Gamma$ of propositions and every proposition $A$,
the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable from $T$ iff every Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms
with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ that makes every member of $T$ and every member of $\Gamma$ true
also makes $A$ true.

articles.title: Strong completeness of classical propositional natural deduction
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a classical
theory, that is, one that derives $\neg\neg B \to B$ for every proposition $B$, where $\neg B$
abbreviates $B \to \bot$. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite set of propositions and $A$ a proposition. If
every Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ that makes every member of
$T$ and every member of $\Gamma$ true also makes $A$ true, then the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is
derivable from $T$.

articles.title: Truth lemma for propositional natural deduction
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be an intuitionistic theory, that
is, one that derives $\bot \to B$ for every proposition $B$. Let $M$ be a set of propositions that
is consistent relative to $T$ and not properly contained in any other set consistent relative to
$T$, and let $v_M$ be the valuation that makes an atom $x$ true exactly when the atomic
proposition $x$ belongs to $M$. Then a proposition $A$ evaluates to true under $v_M$ iff
$A \in M$.

articles.title: Truth value of a negation
articles.statement:
Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let
$v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then for every proposition
$A$, the truth-table value under $v$ of $\neg A$, defined as $A \to \bot$, is the Boolean negation
of the truth-table value of $A$ under $v$.

articles.title: Classical derivability implies truth under valuations with false falsum
articles.statement:
Suppose the atoms
include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with
$v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in classical propositional
logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation
elimination) and every member of $\Gamma$ is true under $v$, then $A$ is true under $v$.

articles.title: Intuitionistic derivability implies truth under valuations with false falsum
articles.statement:
Suppose the
atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with
$v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in intuitionistic
propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\bot \to B$ of ex falso)
and every member of $\Gamma$ is true under $v$, then $A$ is true under $v$.

articles.title: Double-negation elimination is true when falsum is false
articles.statement:
Suppose the atoms include a
distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with
$v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then every instance $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation elimination,
that is every axiom of classical propositional logic, is true under $v$.

articles.title: Ex falso is true when falsum is false
articles.statement:
Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom
$\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then every
instance $\bot \to B$ of ex falso, that is every axiom of intuitionistic propositional logic, is
true under $v$.

articles.title: Truth-table evaluation
articles.statement:
Given a Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms, the truth value of a
proposition is computed recursively: an atom $x$ has value $v(x)$, $A \wedge B$ is true iff both
$A$ and $B$ are, $A \vee B$ is true iff at least one of them is, and $A \to B$ is true iff $A$ is
false or $B$ is true. Falsum $\bot$, when present, is itself an atom, so its value $v(\bot)$ is
part of the valuation and need not be false.

articles.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for propositional natural deduction
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory. Every set
$S$ of propositions that is consistent relative to $T$ is contained in a set $M$ that is
consistent relative to $T$ and not properly contained in any other set consistent relative to
$T$.

articles.title: Propositions outside a maximal consistent set are refuted by it
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory and
$M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. If a proposition $A$ is not in $M$,
then there is a finite set $\Gamma \subseteq M$ such that the sequent
$\Gamma \cup \{A\} \vdash \bot$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$.

articles.title: Maximal consistent sets are deductively closed in propositional natural deduction
articles.statement:
Let $T$
be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. If $\Gamma$ is a
finite subset of $M$ and the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$,
then $A \in M$.

articles.title: Each proposition or its negation lies in a maximal consistent set
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory and
$M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. Then for every proposition $A$,
either $A \in M$ or $\neg A \in M$, where $\neg A$ is the proposition $A \to \bot$.

articles.title: Classical logic proves no atom
articles.statement:
Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$. For
every atom $x$, including $\bot$, the proposition $x$ is not derivable from the empty context in
classical propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\neg\neg B \to B$
of double-negation elimination).

articles.title: Consistency of classical propositional logic
articles.statement:
For every type of atoms with a designated
atom $\bot$, the proposition $\bot$ is not derivable from the empty context in natural deduction
over the classical theory, whose axioms are all instances $\neg\neg A \to A$ of double-negation
elimination, where $\neg A$ abbreviates $A \to \bot$.

articles.title: A maximal consistent set contains its theory
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of
propositions consistent relative to $T$. Then every proposition of $T$ belongs to $M$, that is,
$T \subseteq M$.

articles.title: Lifting lemma
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $x$ a variable and $b$ a Boolean value. If a
clause $D$ is derivable by resolution from the restriction of $\varphi$ by the literal $(x, b)$,
then some clause $D_0$ is derivable by resolution from $\varphi$ such that every literal of $D_0$
is either a literal of $D$ or the complementary literal $(x, \lnot b)$.

articles.title: Clauses of a restricted formula
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $\ell$ a literal. A
clause $C$ belongs to the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if there is a clause $C_0$
of $\varphi$ that does not contain $\ell$ such that $C$ is the restriction of $C_0$ by $\ell$.

articles.title: Unsatisfiable formulas without variables contain the empty clause
articles.statement:
If a CNF formula
$\varphi$ has no variables and is not satisfiable, then the empty clause is one of the clauses
of $\varphi$.

articles.title: Refutable formulas are unsatisfiable
articles.statement:
If the empty clause is derivable by resolution
from a CNF formula $\varphi$, then $\varphi$ is not satisfiable.

articles.title: Soundness and refutation completeness
articles.statement:
A CNF formula has a resolution refutation
iff it is unsatisfiable.

articles.title: Refutation completeness
articles.statement:
**Refutation completeness** of resolution: every unsatisfiable CNF formula has a
resolution derivation of the empty clause.

articles.title: Resolution derivability
articles.statement:
Given a CNF formula $\varphi$, the clauses derivable from
$\varphi$ by resolution form the smallest set $S$ of clauses that contains every clause of
$\varphi$ and, for every variable $x$ and all clauses $C, D \in S$ such that $C$ contains the
literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ and $D$ contains the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$, contains the
resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.

articles.title: Resolvent of two clauses
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. The resolvent of $C$
and $D$ on $x$ is the clause consisting of the literals of $C$ other than $(x, \mathrm{true})$,
in order, followed by the literals of $D$ other than $(x, \mathrm{false})$, in order.

articles.title: Resolution rule soundness
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. Every assignment
that satisfies both $C$ and $D$ satisfies the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.

articles.title: Soundness of resolution
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula. Every clause derivable by
resolution from $\varphi$ is satisfied by every assignment that satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: One step of the linear-time Tseitin builder
articles.statement:
Let $c$ map a gate literal and two operand
literals to a list of clauses, and let $(a, \varphi_A, k_A)$ and $(b, \varphi_B, k_B)$ be the
results for the two operands, each a literal, a clause list and a next free gate number. The step
returns the positive literal $g$ of the variable $2k_B + 1$, the clause list $c(g, a, b)$ followed
by $\varphi_B$, and the next free gate number $k_B + 1$. Neither $\varphi_A$ nor $k_A$ is used: in
the builder, $\varphi_B$ is the accumulator, which already holds both operands' clauses.

articles.title: Allowed variables for a gate range
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, a variable
$x \in \mathbb{N}$ is allowed for the gate range $[k, k')$ if $x$ is even (it names an atom) or
$x$ is a gate in range $[k, k')$, that is, $x = 2j + 1$ for some $j \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$k \le j < k'$.

articles.title: Tseitin clauses for a conjunction
articles.statement:
For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of
the gate literal $g$ for the conjunction of $a$ and $b$ are, in this order, the three clauses
$\lnot g \lor a$, $\lnot g \lor b$ and $g \lor \lnot a \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the
complementary literal of $\ell$ (same variable, opposite polarity).

articles.title: Functions of the atom variables
articles.statement:
A function $f$ from assignments
$\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ to Booleans depends only on the atom variables if
$f(\sigma) = f(\tau)$ for all assignments $\sigma$ and $\tau$ with $\sigma(2n) = \tau(2n)$ for
every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Value of a proposition read off the atom variables
articles.statement:
Given a map $\iota$ from atoms to
natural numbers, a proposition $A$ and an assignment $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$,
this is the truth value of $A$ under the valuation that gives each atom $a$ the value
$\sigma(2\iota(a))$.

articles.title: Equisatisfiability of the Tseitin transformation
articles.statement:
Let the atoms have a distinguished atom
$\bot$, let $\iota$ be an injective map from atoms to natural numbers and let $A$ be a
proposition. The Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$, together with the unit clause making
the variable $2\iota(\bot)$ false, is satisfiable if and only if $A$ is true under some valuation
$v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot)$ false.

articles.title: Connective count of a propositional formula
articles.statement:
For a propositional formula $A$, built from
atoms with the binary connectives $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\to$, the connective count of $A$ is the
number of occurrences of these connectives in $A$. It is $0$ for an atom, and for $B \circ C$,
with $\circ$ one of $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\to$, it is the count of $B$ plus the count of $C$
plus $1$.

articles.title: Tseitin correctness
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be an injective map from atoms to natural numbers, let
$A$ be a proposition and let $v$ be a valuation of the atoms. Then $A$ is true under $v$ if and
only if some assignment $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ with $\sigma(2\iota(a)) = v(a)$
for every atom $a$ satisfies the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$.

articles.title: Tseitin clauses for an implication
articles.statement:
For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of
the gate literal $g$ for the implication from $a$ to $b$ are, in this order, the three clauses
$\lnot g \lor \lnot a \lor b$, $g \lor a$ and $g \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the
complementary literal of $\ell$ (same variable, opposite polarity).

articles.title: Gate variables in a range
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, a variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$
is a gate in range $[k, k')$ if $x = 2j + 1$ for some $j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \le j < k'$.

articles.title: Tseitin clauses have at most three literals
articles.statement:
For every proposition $A$ and every map
$\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, every clause of the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to
$\iota$ has at most three literals.

articles.title: Number of defining clauses in the Tseitin encoding
articles.statement:
For every map $\iota$ from atoms to
natural numbers, every formula $A$ and every gate number $k$, the list of defining clauses
produced by the Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$ has length $3c$, where $c$ is
the number of binary connectives of $A$.

articles.title: Number of clauses of the Tseitin CNF
articles.statement:
For every proposition $A$ and every map $\iota$
from atoms to natural numbers, the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$, as a list of
clauses counted with repetition, has length $3c + 1$, where $c$ is the number of binary
connectives of $A$: three defining clauses per connective plus the unit clause asserting $A$.

articles.title: Truth value of a literal
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ assign a Boolean value to every natural-number
variable, and let $\ell = (x, b)$ be a literal with variable $x$ and polarity $b$. The truth
value of $\ell$ under $\sigma$ is true exactly when $\sigma(x) = b$.

articles.title: Complementary literal
articles.statement:
The complement of a literal $(x, b)$ with variable $x$ and
polarity $b$ is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$: the same variable with the opposite polarity.

articles.title: Tseitin clauses for a disjunction
articles.statement:
For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses
of the gate literal $g$ for the disjunction of $a$ and $b$ are the three clauses
$\lnot g \lor a \lor b$, $g \lor \lnot a$ and $g \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the
complementary literal of $\ell$.

articles.title: Satisfying a concatenation of CNF formulas
articles.statement:
For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean
values to the natural-number variables and all CNF formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $\sigma$
satisfies the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$ followed by those of $\psi$ if
and only if $\sigma$ satisfies both $\varphi$ and $\psi$.

articles.title: Satisfaction depends only on the occurring variables
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and
let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be assignments of Boolean values to the natural-number variables that
agree on every variable occurring in a literal of $\varphi$. If $\sigma$ satisfies $\varphi$,
then $\tau$ satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: Correctness invariant of the Tseitin encoding
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ map atoms to natural numbers,
let $A$ be a proposition and $k$ a natural number, and let $(\ell, \Phi, k')$ be the reference
Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$: the literal naming $A$, its defining
clauses and the next unused gate number. For an assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the
natural-number variables, let $A[\sigma]$ be the truth value of $A$ when each atom $a$ gets
the value $\sigma(2\iota(a))$, and call a variable a gate in range if it equals $2j + 1$ for
some $j$ with $k \le j < k'$. Then $k \le k'$; the variable of $\ell$ and every variable
occurring in a literal of $\Phi$ is even or a gate in range; every assignment $\sigma$ that
satisfies $\Phi$ gives $\ell$ the value $A[\sigma]$; and for every assignment $\sigma$ there is
an assignment $\tau$ that agrees with $\sigma$ on every variable that is not a gate in range,
satisfies $\Phi$ and gives $\ell$ the value $A[\sigma]$.

articles.title: Tseitin encoding invariant
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $r = (\ell, \Phi, k')$
consist of a literal $\ell$, a CNF formula $\Phi$ and a natural number $k'$, and let $v$ map
each assignment of Boolean values to the natural-number variables to a Boolean value. Call a
variable a gate in range if it equals $2j + 1$ for some $j$ with $k \le j < k'$. The invariant
holds for $k$, $r$ and $v$ when $k \le k'$; the variable of $\ell$ and every variable occurring
in a literal of $\Phi$ is even or a gate in range; every assignment $\sigma$ that satisfies
$\Phi$ gives $\ell$ the value $v(\sigma)$; and for every assignment $\sigma$ there is an
assignment $\tau$ that agrees with $\sigma$ on every variable that is not a gate in range,
satisfies $\Phi$ and gives $\ell$ the value $v(\sigma)$.

Here $r$ is meant to be the result (literal, clauses, next gate) of encoding a proposition with
gates numbered from $k$, and $v$ the value of that proposition.

articles.title: The linear-time Tseitin builder agrees with the reference encoding
articles.statement:
For every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, every formula $A$, every gate number $k$
and every clause list $\mathit{acc}$, the linear-time Tseitin builder run on $A$ from gate $k$
with accumulator $\mathit{acc}$ returns the same literal naming $A$ and the same next unused
gate number as the reference Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$, and its
clause list is $X$ followed by $\mathit{acc}$ for some list of clauses $X$ that is a
permutation of the defining clauses of the reference encoding.

articles.title: Linear-time Tseitin builder
articles.statement:
Fix a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers. Given a
formula $A$, a gate number $k$ and a clause list $\mathit{acc}$, the builder returns a literal
naming $A$, a clause list and the next unused gate number. For an atom $a$ it returns the
positive literal of variable $2\iota(a)$, the list $\mathit{acc}$ unchanged, and $k$. For
$A \circ B$ with $\circ$ one of $\wedge$, $\vee$, $\to$, it runs on $A$ from gate $k$ with
accumulator $\mathit{acc}$, obtaining a literal $a$, a list $L_A$ and a gate number $k'$, then on
$B$ from gate $k'$ with accumulator $L_A$, obtaining $b$, $L_B$ and $k''$; it returns the positive
literal $g$ of variable $2k''+1$, the three defining clauses of $g$ for $a \circ b$ followed by
$L_B$, and $k''+1$.

Unlike the reference Tseitin encoding, which concatenates the operands' clause lists, it
prepends each gate's clauses to the accumulator, so it runs in linear time and the clauses come
out in a different order.

articles.title: Tseitin encoding with gates numbered from $k$
articles.statement:
Fix a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural
numbers. Given a formula $A$ and a gate number $k$, the encoding returns a literal naming $A$, a
list of defining clauses and the next unused gate number. For an atom $a$ it returns the
positive literal of variable $2\iota(a)$, no clauses, and $k$. For $A \circ B$ with $\circ$ one of
$\wedge$, $\vee$, $\to$, it encodes $A$ from gate $k$, obtaining a literal $a$, clauses $C_A$ and a
gate number $k'$, then $B$ from gate $k'$, obtaining $b$, $C_B$ and $k''$; it returns the positive
literal $g$ of variable $2k''+1$, the clauses $C_A$, then $C_B$, then the three defining clauses
of $g$ for $a \circ b$, and $k''+1$.

Its list concatenations make it quadratic; the Tseitin CNF is computed by a linear-time builder
that produces the same clauses in another order.

articles.title: Tseitin CNF with $\bot$ false
articles.statement:
For an atom type with a distinguished atom $\bot$, a map
$\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and a formula $A$, this is the CNF consisting of the unit
clause whose literal is the negative literal of variable $2\iota(\bot)$, followed by the Tseitin
CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$.
