articles.title: The Tseitin CNF reorders the reference encoding
articles.statement:
For every map $\iota$ from atoms to
natural numbers and every formula $A$, the Tseitin CNF of $A$ is the unit clause whose literal
is the literal naming $A$ in the reference Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $0$,
followed by a list of clauses that is a permutation of the defining clauses of that encoding.

articles.title: One step of the Tseitin encoding
articles.statement:
Given a rule $\mathit{cl}$ assigning to literals $g$, $a$,
$b$ a list of defining clauses, and the results $(a, C_A, k_A)$ and $(b, C_B, k_B)$ of encoding
the two operands of a binary connective (each a literal, a clause list and a next unused gate
number), the step returns the positive literal $g$ of variable $2k_B+1$, the clause list $C_A$,
then $C_B$, then $\mathit{cl}(g, a, b)$, and the next gate number $k_B+1$.

articles.title: Tseitin CNF
articles.statement:
For a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and a formula $A$, run the
linear-time Tseitin builder on $A$ with gates numbered from $0$ and the empty accumulator,
obtaining a literal $\ell$ naming $A$ and a clause list $C$. The Tseitin CNF of $A$ is the unit
clause $[\ell]$ followed by $C$.

articles.title: One-state Büchi automaton for always φ
articles.statement:
The one-state Büchi automaton for `G φ` with `φ` propositional: it stays
forever, requiring every letter to satisfy `φ`.

articles.title: Evaluating a propositional formula at a letter
articles.statement:
A letter is a set $s$ of atoms (the
atoms true at it). A propositional formula is evaluated at $s$ by recursion: an atom $a$ is true
iff $a \in s$, truth $\top$ is true, $\neg\varphi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is not, and
$\varphi \wedge \psi$ is true iff both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are true.

articles.title: Büchi automata for the restricted safety fragment
articles.statement:
Take as letters the sets of atoms,
an atom $a$ holding at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$. For every formula $\psi$ of the restricted
safety fragment there is a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states whose
ω-language is exactly the set of infinite words satisfying $\psi$, read as an LTL formula.

The finite state set is what makes the automaton a certificate of ω-regularity: every
ω-language is accepted by some Büchi automaton with infinitely many states. The fragment applies
the always operator $\mathbf{G}$ only to propositional formulas, so for example
$\mathbf{G}(p \vee \mathbf{X}\,q)$, for atoms $p$ and $q$ and the next operator $\mathbf{X}$, is
not covered.

articles.title: The infinitely-often automaton recognizes G F φ
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a propositional
formula and $p$ the set of letters (sets of atoms) at which $\varphi$ evaluates to true. The
two-state Büchi automaton for “infinitely often $p$” accepts exactly the infinite words that
satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$
iff $a \in s$. Equivalently, a word is accepted iff $\varphi$ holds at infinitely many positions.

articles.title: The always automaton recognizes G φ
articles.statement:
For a propositional formula $\varphi$, the
one-state Büchi automaton for $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ accepts exactly the infinite words of letters
(sets of atoms) that satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a
letter $s$ iff $a \in s$.

articles.title: The eventually-always automaton recognizes F G φ
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a propositional
formula and $p$ the set of letters (sets of atoms) at which $\varphi$ evaluates to true. The
two-state Büchi automaton for “eventually always $p$” accepts exactly the infinite words that
satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$
iff $a \in s$. Equivalently, a word is accepted iff $\varphi$ holds at all but finitely many
positions.

articles.title: The propositional automaton recognizes φ
articles.statement:
For a propositional formula $\varphi$, the
three-state Büchi automaton for $\varphi$ accepts exactly the infinite words of letters (sets of
atoms) that satisfy $\varphi$ read as an LTL formula, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff
$a \in s$.

articles.title: The shift automaton reads the tail
articles.statement:
For a Büchi automaton $A$ over letters that are sets
of atoms, the shift automaton of $A$ accepts an infinite word $x_0 x_1 x_2 \ldots$ iff $A$
accepts its tail $x_1 x_2 x_3 \ldots$.

articles.title: Propositional formulas
articles.statement:
The propositional formulas over a set of atoms are generated by
the atoms, the constant truth $\top$, negation $\neg\varphi$ and conjunction
$\varphi \wedge \psi$.

articles.title: Büchi automaton for a propositional formula
articles.statement:
For a propositional formula $\varphi$, this
Büchi automaton over letters that are sets of atoms has a start state $u$ and two verdict states
$t$ and $f$, of which only $t$ is accepting. From $u$, on a letter $s$ it moves to $t$ if
$\varphi$ evaluates to true at $s$ and to $f$ otherwise; from $t$ and from $f$ it stays in the
same state on every letter. So it records the verdict of $\varphi$ on the first letter.

articles.title: The restricted safety fragment of LTL
articles.statement:
The safety formulas over a type of atoms are
generated by the following rules: every propositional formula $\varphi$ is a safety formula; if
$\psi$ and $\rho$ are safety formulas, then so are $\psi \wedge \rho$, $\psi \vee \rho$ and
$X\,\psi$ (next $\psi$); and for every propositional formula $\varphi$, $G\,\varphi$ (always
$\varphi$) is a safety formula.

The operator $G$ is applied only to propositional formulas: for atoms $p$ and $q$, the formula
$G(p \vee X\,q)$ is not in this fragment, since $G$ does not distribute over $\vee$.

articles.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the current letter
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a
propositional formula, let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of atoms,
and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Under the valuation in which an atom holds at a letter exactly when it
belongs to that letter, the LTL translation of $\varphi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ if and only
if $\varphi$ evaluates to true on the letter $w_k$.

articles.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the first letter
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a
propositional formula and let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of
atoms. Under the valuation in which an atom holds at a letter exactly when it belongs to that
letter, $w$ satisfies the LTL translation of $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ evaluates to true
on the first letter $w_0$.

articles.title: The shift of a Büchi automaton
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Büchi automaton over the alphabet of sets of
atoms. Its shift is the Büchi automaton whose states are the states of $A$ together with one new
state $\bot$, whose only start state is $\bot$, and whose accepting states are the accepting states
of $A$. Its transitions are exactly the following: on every letter, from $\bot$ to each start state
of $A$; and on a letter $x$, from a state $q$ of $A$ to a state $q'$ of $A$ whenever $A$ has a
transition from $q$ to $q'$ on $x$.

The shift accepts a word exactly when $A$ accepts the word with its first letter removed.

articles.title: Safety formulas as LTL formulas
Propositional formulas as LTL formulas
articles.statement:
The translation of propositional formulas into LTL
formulas is defined by recursion: an atom $a$ goes to the LTL atom $a$, truth goes to the LTL
truth constant $\top$, $\neg\varphi$ goes to the LTL negation of the translation of $\varphi$, and
$\varphi \wedge \psi$ goes to the LTL conjunction of the translations of $\varphi$ and $\psi$.

articles.title: Falsity in CTL
articles.statement:
The CTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) is the negation $\neg\top$ of the formula
$\top$ (truth).

articles.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ is a least fixed point
articles.statement:
Fix a labelled transition system, a valuation of the
atoms at its states, and a CTL formula $\varphi$. Write $[\![\varphi]\!]$ for the set of states
satisfying $\varphi$ and $\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ for the set of states having some successor in a
set of states $Z$. Then the set of states satisfying $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ is the least fixed point
of the monotone operator $Z \mapsto [\![\varphi]\!] \cup \mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ on sets of states.

The fixed point is contained in $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ by Park induction, using the one-step
expansion of $\mathsf{EF}$; the converse is induction on a path to a $\varphi$-state, unfolding the
fixed point once per step.

articles.title: One-step expansion of $\mathsf{EF}$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled
transition system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ if and only if $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ or $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{EX}\,\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$, that is, some successor of $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$.

articles.title: The $\mathsf{EF}$ functional
articles.statement:
Given a labelled transition system, a valuation of the atoms
at its states, and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the map sending a set of states $Z$ to the set
of states that satisfy $\varphi$ or have some successor in $Z$.

Its least fixed point is the set of states satisfying $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$.

articles.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ means reachability
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled transition
system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ if
and only if some state $t$ reachable from $s$ by a finite, possibly empty, sequence of transitions
satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ via finite runs
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled transition
system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ if
and only if there are a sequence of states $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ with $s_0 = s$ and a natural
number $k$ such that the sequence is a finite run of length $k$ and $s_k$ satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: The $\mathsf{EF}$ operator
articles.statement:
Given a labelled transition system, a valuation of the atoms at
its states, and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the monotone operator on sets of states, ordered by
inclusion, sending a set $Z$ to the set of states that satisfy $\varphi$ or have some successor in
$Z$.

articles.title: Exists finally
articles.statement:
For a CTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ is the
existential until $\mathsf{E}[\top \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \varphi]$ with $\top$ on the left.

A state satisfies $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ exactly when some state reachable from it satisfies
$\varphi$.

articles.title: $\mathsf{EG}$ is a greatest fixed point
articles.statement:
Fix a labelled transition system, a valuation of
the atoms at its states, and a CTL formula $\varphi$. Write $[\![\varphi]\!]$ for the set of states
satisfying $\varphi$ and $\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ for the set of states having some successor in a
set of states $Z$. Then the set of states satisfying $\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$ is the greatest fixed
point of the monotone operator $Z \mapsto [\![\varphi]\!] \cap \mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ on sets of
states.

The inclusion of $\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$ in the fixed point is coinduction, using the one-step
expansion of $\mathsf{EG}$. The converse builds an infinite run by repeatedly choosing a successor
inside the fixed point, so it uses the axiom of choice.

articles.title: One-step expansion of $\mathsf{EG}$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled
transition system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$ if and only if $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{EX}\,\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$, that is, some successor of $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$.

Both directions are direct manipulations of infinite runs; no choice is needed.

articles.title: The functional for $\mathrm{EG}$
articles.statement:
Given a labelled transition system, a valuation of
the atoms and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the operator that sends a predicate $Z$ on states
to the predicate holding at a state $s$ when $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and some successor of $s$
satisfies $Z$, that is, there are a label $a$ and a state $t$ with a transition from $s$ to $t$
labelled $a$ such that $Z$ holds at $t$.

Its greatest fixed point is the set of states satisfying $\mathrm{EG}\,\varphi$.

articles.title: The $\mathrm{EG}$ functional as a monotone operator
articles.statement:
Given a labelled transition system,
a valuation of the atoms and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the monotone map on predicates on
states, ordered pointwise by implication, that sends a predicate $Z$ to the predicate holding at
a state $s$ when $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and some successor of $s$ satisfies $Z$.

articles.title: Finite runs extend to infinite runs in serial systems
articles.statement:
In a serial labelled transition
system, if $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ is a finite run of length $k$, then there is an infinite run
$s'_0, s'_1, s'_2, \dots$ with $s'_i = s_i$ for every $i \le k$.

The extension iterates a chosen successor function from $s_k$, so it uses the axiom of choice.

articles.title: One-step expansion of $\mathrm{EU}$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL formulas and $s$ a
state of a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms. Then $s$ satisfies
$\mathrm{E}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathrm{U}} \psi]$ if and only if either $s$ satisfies $\psi$, or
$s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and some successor of $s$ satisfies
$\mathrm{E}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathrm{U}} \psi]$.

articles.title: $\mathrm{AF}$ at a deadlocked state
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula and $s$ a state of a
labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms. If $s$ has no outgoing transition,
then $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{AF}\,\varphi$ if and only if $s$ satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: On serial systems $\mathrm{AF}$ is $\neg\mathrm{EG}\,\neg$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CTL
formula and $s$ a state of a serial labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms.
Then $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{AF}\,\varphi$ if and only if $s$ does not satisfy
$\mathrm{EG}\,\neg\varphi$.

A serial system has no deadlocked states, so every maximal path is infinite and $\mathrm{AF}$
recovers its classical form.

articles.title: Maximal-path form of $\mathrm{AF}$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula and $s$ a state of a
labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms. Then $s$ satisfies
$\mathrm{AF}\,\varphi$ if and only if both of the following hold: for every infinite run
$s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ with $s_0 = s$ there is some $k$ such that $s_k$ satisfies $\varphi$; and
for every finite run $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ of length $k$ with $s_0 = s$ whose endpoint $s_k$
has no outgoing transition, there is some $j \le k$ such that $s_j$ satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: The CTL operator AF (inevitably)
articles.statement:
`AF φ`: every maximal path reaches a state satisfying `φ`, as
`A[⊤ U φ]`.

articles.title: $\mathrm{AG}$ holds iff every reachable state satisfies the formula
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ be a
CTL formula and $s$ a state of a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms.
Then $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{AG}\,\varphi$ if and only if every state $t$ reachable from $s$
(through a finite sequence of transitions, possibly empty) satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: The CTL operator $\mathrm{AG}$
articles.statement:
For a CTL formula $\varphi$, the formula
$\mathrm{AG}\,\varphi$ is $\neg\,\mathrm{EF}\,\neg\varphi$. It holds at a state exactly when
every state reachable from it satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: Characterization of $\mathsf{AX}$
articles.statement:
Let $s$ be a state of a labelled transition system
with an atom valuation, and let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. Then $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{AX}\,\varphi$ if and only if every state $t$ with a transition from $s$ to $t$, under
any label, satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: The CTL operator $\mathsf{AX}$
articles.statement:
For a CTL formula $\varphi$, the formula
$\mathsf{AX}\,\varphi$ ("on all next states, $\varphi$") is defined as
$\neg\,\mathsf{EX}\,\neg\varphi$.

It holds at a state exactly when every successor of that state satisfies $\varphi$, so it holds
vacuously at a deadlocked state.

articles.title: $\mathsf{A}(\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi)$ at a deadlocked state
articles.statement:
Let $s$ be a state of a
labelled transition system with an atom valuation, and suppose that $s$ is deadlocked: there is
no transition from $s$ under any label. Then for all CTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $s$
satisfies $\mathsf{A}[\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi]$ if and only if $s$ satisfies $\psi$.

The infinite-run condition is vacuous, since an infinite run needs a step at index $0$, and the
constant finite run of length $0$ forces $\psi$ at $s$ itself.

articles.title: Classical form of $\mathsf{A}(\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi)$ on serial systems
articles.statement:
Let $s$ be a
state of a serial labelled transition system with an atom valuation, and let $\varphi$ and $\psi$
be CTL formulas. Then $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{A}[\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi]$ if and only if $s$
satisfies neither $\mathsf{E}[\neg\psi\,\mathsf{U}\,(\neg\varphi \land \neg\psi)]$ nor
$\mathsf{EG}\,\neg\psi$. That is, no finite run from $s$ ends at a state satisfying
$\neg\varphi \land \neg\psi$ with $\neg\psi$ at all earlier states, and no infinite run from $s$
has $\neg\psi$ at every state.

The forward direction extends an $\mathsf{EU}$ witness to an infinite run; the backward
direction takes, on each infinite run, the least $\psi$-position and derives an $\mathsf{EU}$
witness from any earlier $\neg\varphi$-position.

articles.title: CTL formulas
articles.statement:
The formulas of computation tree logic over a type $A$ of atoms are
generated as follows: every atom $a \in A$ is a formula, $\top$ is a formula, and if $\varphi$
and $\psi$ are formulas then so are the negation $\neg\varphi$, the conjunction
$\varphi \land \psi$, the existential next $\mathsf{EX}\,\varphi$, the existential until
$\mathsf{E}[\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi]$, the existential globally $\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$ and the
universal until $\mathsf{A}[\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi]$.

The universal until is primitive rather than the classical translation through $\mathsf{EU}$
and $\mathsf{EG}$, which is unsound on transition systems with deadlocked states.

articles.title: CTL bi-implication
articles.statement:
For CTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the bi-implication
$\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ is defined as the conjunction $(\varphi \to \psi) \land
(\psi \to \varphi)$ of the two implications.

articles.title: CTL implication
articles.statement:
For CTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the implication
$\varphi \to \psi$ is defined as the disjunction $\neg\varphi \lor \psi$.

articles.title: CTL disjunction
articles.statement:
For CTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the disjunction
$\varphi \lor \psi$ is defined as $
eg(
eg\varphi \land 
eg\psi)$.

articles.title: Existential predecessor operator
articles.statement:
For a labelled transition system and a predicate $Z$
on its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ when some successor of $s$
satisfies $Z$: there are a label $a$ and a state $t$ satisfying $Z$ with a transition from $s$
to $t$ labelled $a$.

articles.title: Satisfaction of CTL formulas
articles.statement:
Fix a labelled transition system and a valuation saying
which atoms hold at which states. Satisfaction of a CTL formula at a state $s$ is defined by
recursion on the formula. An atom $a$ holds at $s$ when the valuation makes $a$ true at $s$;
$\top$ always holds; $\neg\varphi$ holds when $\varphi$ does not; $\varphi \land \psi$ holds
when both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ hold; $\mathsf{EX}\,\varphi$ holds when there is a transition
from $s$, under some label, to a state satisfying $\varphi$; $\mathsf{E}[\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi]$
holds when some finite run $s = s_0, s_1, \dots, s_k$ has $\psi$ at $s_k$ and $\varphi$ at every
$s_j$ with $j < k$; $\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$ holds when some infinite run $s = s_0, s_1, \dots$ has
$\varphi$ at every state; and $\mathsf{A}[\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi]$ holds when, first, every
infinite run $s = s_0, s_1, \dots$ has some $k$ with $\psi$ at $s_k$ and $\varphi$ at every $s_j$
with $j < k$, and second, every finite run $s = s_0, s_1, \dots, s_k$ whose last state $s_k$ has
no outgoing transition under any label has some $j \le k$ with $\psi$ at $s_j$ and $\varphi$ at
every $s_i$ with $i < j$.

articles.title: Serial transition systems
articles.statement:
A labelled transition system is serial (total) when every
state $s$ has a successor: there are a label $a$ and a state $t$ with a transition from $s$ to
$t$ labelled $a$.

A serial system has no deadlocked states, and every maximal path in it is infinite.

articles.title: Always operator on CTL$^{\ast}$ path formulas
articles.statement: `G π`: `π` holds at every position, as `¬(⊤ U ¬π)`.

articles.title: The CTL embedding preserves semantics on serial systems
articles.statement: The CTL embedding preserves semantics on serial systems.

articles.title: Embedding of CTL formulas as CTL$^{\ast}$ state formulas
articles.statement:
The CTL embedding: every CTL formula is a CTL* state formula.
`EG φ` is `E G (state φ)`; `AU` is `A (state φ U state ψ)`.

articles.title: The LTL embedding preserves semantics at every position
articles.statement:
The structural LTL embedding also agrees at every position,
without assuming the sequence is a valid transition run.

articles.title: The LTL embedding preserves semantics on every sequence
articles.statement:
The LTL embedding preserves semantics on every state sequence,
including sequences that are not valid runs of `lts`.

articles.title: Embedding of LTL formulas as CTL$^{\ast}$ path formulas
articles.statement: The LTL embedding: every LTL formula is a CTL* path formula.

articles.title: Eventually operator on CTL$^{\ast}$ path formulas
articles.statement: `F π`: `π` holds at some position, as `⊤ U π`.

articles.title: Path formulas of CTL$^{\ast}$
articles.statement:
Path formulas of CTL*: a state formula at the first position,
negation, conjunction, `next`, and `until`.

articles.title: Always holds on a run iff its argument holds on every suffix
articles.statement: `G π` holds on a run iff `π` holds on every suffix.

articles.title: Eventually holds on a run iff its argument holds on some suffix
articles.statement: `F π` holds on a run iff `π` holds on some suffix.

articles.title: Next on a run is satisfaction on the shifted run
articles.statement: Unfolding: `next` shifts the run.

articles.title: A state formula on a shifted run holds at the shifted state
articles.statement:
A state formula on a shifted run is satisfaction at the shifted
position.

articles.title: A state formula on a run holds at its first state
articles.statement:
Unfolding: a state formula on a run is satisfaction at its first
state.

articles.title: Satisfaction of CTL$^{\ast}$ path formulas on infinite runs
articles.statement:
Satisfaction of a CTL* path formula on an infinite run: `next`
shifts the run, `until` asks for a target position with the guard
before it.

articles.title: A run shifted by k starts at its k-th state
articles.statement:
`(shiftSeq run k) 0 = run k`: the `0 + k` is discharged by
`Nat.zero_add`.

articles.title: State formulas of CTL$^{\ast}$
articles.statement:
State formulas of CTL*: atoms, truth, negation, conjunction, and
the path quantifiers `E π` and `A π`.

articles.title: Satisfaction of CTL$^{\ast}$ state formulas
articles.statement:
Satisfaction of a CTL* state formula at a state: `E π` holds when
some infinite run from the state satisfies `π`; `A π` when every
infinite run does.

articles.title: $E\,G\,F\,p$ holds at false in the toggle system
articles.statement:
`E G F p` holds at `false` in the toggle system: the alternating
run visits `true` at every other position. This example makes no claim
of an expressiveness separation.

articles.title: Toggle transition system
articles.statement: The toggle system: every transition flips the state.

articles.title: Alternating run of the toggle system
articles.statement:
The alternating run of the toggle system: `false, true, false,
true, ...`, defined by recursion so each step flips the state.

articles.title: The toggle system is serial
articles.statement: The toggle system is serial: every state has a successor.

articles.title: Valuation of the toggle system
articles.statement: The valuation: `p` holds exactly at `true`.

articles.title: CTL* state-sequence/execution bridge, path formulas
articles.statement:
**CTL* state-sequence/execution bridge, path formulas.** CTL* path
satisfaction on a state run agrees with the canonical labeled-execution
presentation on the same state sequence.

articles.title: CTL* state-sequence/execution bridge, state formulas
articles.statement:
**CTL* state-sequence/execution bridge, state formulas.** CTL* state satisfaction
over `lts` agrees with satisfaction quantified over canonical `OmegaExecution`s.

articles.title: CTL$^{\ast}$ path satisfaction on labeled executions
articles.statement:
Satisfaction of a CTL* path formula on a canonical infinite labeled execution:
`next` drops the first state, while `until` asks for a target position with the guard
before it.

articles.title: CTL$^{\ast}$ state satisfaction over labeled executions
No existential path formula holds at a terminal state
articles.statement: No existential infinite path formula holds at a terminal state.

articles.title: Universal path formulas hold vacuously at terminal states
articles.statement: Universal infinite path quantification is vacuous at a terminal state.

articles.title: Idempotence of always
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and
every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$
if and only if it satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{G}$ is the always
operator.

articles.title: Always eventually means infinitely often
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters,
every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies
$\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (always eventually $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there are
infinitely many $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies
$\varphi$ under $v$.

articles.title: The always operator of LTL
articles.statement:
For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula
$\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ ("always $\varphi$") is defined as $\neg\,\mathbf{F}\,\neg\varphi$, the
negation of "eventually $\neg\varphi$".

On an ω-word, $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ holds at a position exactly when $\varphi$ holds at that
position and at every later one.

articles.title: Satisfaction of an atom
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$
and every atom $a$, the word $w$ satisfies the atomic formula $a$ under $v$ if and only if $v$
makes $a$ true at the first letter $w_0$ of $w$.

articles.title: Falsity is never satisfied
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters and every
ω-word $w$, the word $w$ does not satisfy the LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) under $v$.

articles.title: Falsity in LTL
articles.statement:
The LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) is defined as $\neg\top$, the negation
of the truth constant $\top$.

articles.title: Eventually always means from some point on
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters,
every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies
$\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ (eventually always $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there is
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \ge n$ the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$
satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

articles.title: Semantics of eventually
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$
and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (eventually
$\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the suffix of $w$ starting at
position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

articles.title: The eventually operator of LTL
articles.statement:
For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula
$\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ ("eventually $\varphi$") is defined as the until formula
$\top \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \varphi$.

On an ω-word, $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ holds at a position exactly when $\varphi$ holds at that
position or at some later one.

articles.title: Formulas of linear temporal logic
articles.statement:
For a type $A$ of atoms, the formulas of linear
temporal logic (LTL) over $A$ are generated inductively: every atom $a \in A$ is a formula, the
truth constant $\top$ is a formula, and if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so are the
negation $\neg\varphi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$, the next formula
$\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ and the until formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \psi$.

articles.title: Bi-implication in LTL
articles.statement:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the bi-implication
$\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ is defined as the conjunction
$(\varphi \to \psi) \wedge (\psi \to \varphi)$ of the two implications.

articles.title: Implication in LTL
articles.statement:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the implication
$\varphi \to \psi$ is defined as the disjunction $\neg\varphi \vee \psi$.

articles.title: Language of an LTL formula
articles.statement:
Given a valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, the ω-language of
an LTL formula $\varphi$ is the set of ω-words that satisfy $\varphi$ under $v$.

articles.title: Membership in the language of a formula
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters,
every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ belongs to the ω-language of
$\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.

articles.title: Next is self-dual
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every
LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\neg\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if
it satisfies $\mathbf{X}\,\neg\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.

articles.title: Disjunction in LTL
articles.statement:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the disjunction
$\varphi \vee \psi$ is defined as $
eg(
eg\varphi \wedge 
eg\psi)$.

articles.title: Expansion law for release
articles.statement:
For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$
and all LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the word $w$ satisfies
$\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$) under $v$ if and only if it
satisfies $\psi$ and it satisfies $\varphi$ or $\mathbf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi)$,
all under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.

articles.title: Semantics of release
articles.statement:
For a valuation of atoms on letters, an ω-word $w$ and LTL formulas
$\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$)
if and only if for every position $k$, either $\psi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ or $\varphi$
holds at some position $j < k$ of $w$.

articles.title: The release operator of LTL
articles.statement:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the release
formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{R}} \psi$ is defined as
$\neg(\neg\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \neg\psi)$, the dual of until.

On an ω-word, $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{R}} \psi$ holds at a position when, from that position on,
$\psi$ holds up to and including the first position where $\varphi$ holds, or forever if there is
no such position.

articles.title: Satisfaction of an atom at a position
articles.statement:
Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an
ω-word, $a$ an atom and $k$ a natural number. The atomic formula $a$ holds at position $k$ of $w$
under $v$ if and only if $v$ makes $a$ true at the letter $w(k)$.

articles.title: Satisfaction on a suffix
articles.statement:
Let $w$ be an ω-word and, for a natural number $k$, let
$w^{(k)}$ be its suffix starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$. For every
valuation of atoms on letters, every LTL formula $\varphi$ and every natural number $j$,
$\varphi$ holds at position $j$ of $w^{(k)}$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at position $k + j$
of $w$.

articles.title: Satisfaction at position zero
articles.statement:
For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL
formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ holds at position $0$ of $w$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$.

articles.title: Satisfaction at a position
articles.statement:
Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an ω-word, $k$
a natural number and $\varphi$ an LTL formula. Then $\varphi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ under
$v$ when the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$, satisfies
$\varphi$ under $v$.

articles.title: Relabelling the letters of an ω-word
articles.statement:
Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters of an
alphabet $\Sigma$, let $f \colon \Sigma' \to \Sigma$ be a map, and let $w$ be an ω-word over
$\Sigma'$. For every LTL formula $\varphi$, the relabelled word $i \mapsto f(w(i))$ satisfies
$\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under the valuation that makes an atom
$a$ true at a letter $s$ of $\Sigma'$ exactly when $v$ makes $a$ true at $f(s)$.

articles.title: Satisfaction of LTL formulas on ω-words
articles.statement:
Let $v$ be a valuation that says which atoms are
true at each letter, and for an ω-word $w$ and a natural number $k$ let $w^{(k)}$ be the suffix
$i \mapsto w(k + i)$. Whether $w$ satisfies an LTL formula $\varphi$ under $v$, written
$w \models \varphi$, is defined by recursion on $\varphi$: an atom $a$ holds when $v$ makes $a$
true at the first letter $w(0)$; truth always holds; $\neg \varphi$ holds when $\varphi$ does
not; $\varphi \wedge \psi$ holds when both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ do; $\mathsf{X}\, \varphi$ (next
$\varphi$) holds when $w^{(1)} \models \varphi$; and $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi$
($\varphi$ until $\psi$) holds when there is a $k$ with $w^{(k)} \models \psi$ and
$w^{(j)} \models \varphi$ for all $j < k$.

articles.title: Expansion law for until
articles.statement:
For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL
formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ until
$\psi$) if and only if either $w$ satisfies $\psi$, or $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ and also satisfies
$\mathsf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi)$, that is, next ($\varphi$ until $\psi$).

articles.title: Closedness of a μ-calculus formula at a binder depth
articles.statement:
`φ` is closed at depth `d` when every free variable is below `d`
(de Bruijn): `var n` needs `n < d`, and binders increase the depth.

articles.title: Closed linear μ-calculus formula
articles.statement: A formula with no free variables.

articles.title: Double complement of a predicate
articles.statement: Complementing a predicate twice returns it.

articles.title: Depth of a linear μ-calculus formula
articles.statement:
The depth of a formula: the length of its longest root-to-leaf path, counting
each connective once.

articles.title: Complementing an environment commutes with extension
articles.statement: Complementing an environment commutes with extending it.

articles.title: Extending an environment under a binder
articles.statement: Extend an environment under a binder (de Bruijn).

articles.title: The linear μ-calculus `F` is eventuality
articles.statement: **The linear μ-calculus `F` is eventuality.**

articles.title: Eventually operator in the linear μ-calculus
articles.statement: `F p`: `p` holds at some future position.

articles.title: The linear μ-calculus `G` is universality over the future
articles.statement: **The linear μ-calculus `G` is universality over the future.**

articles.title: Always operator in the linear μ-calculus
articles.statement: `G p`: `p` holds at every future position.

articles.title: Formula depth is bounded by its code
articles.statement:
A formula's depth is at most its code: pairing dominates each component
(`Nat.add_le_pair`).

articles.title: Injectivity of the linear μ-calculus code
articles.statement: The encoding is injective.

articles.title: Cantor-pairing code of linear μ-calculus formulas
articles.statement:
An injective encoding of linear μ-calculus formulas over `ℕ` atoms as
natural numbers, via the Cantor pairing function `Nat.pair`. This is a Nat
code only, not a complexity input encoding: repeated pairing squares the
code at every unary connective, so the binary length of the code of
`next^d (atom 0)` doubles at each `next` and is exponential in `d`.
Complexity statements use `linearMuTokens` / `linearMuDecodeList` instead.

articles.title: Fuelled decoding inverts encoding
articles.statement: Decoding inverts encoding, with enough fuel.

articles.title: Fuelled decoding of linear μ-calculus codes
articles.statement:
Fuelled decoding of a `linearMuCode` number back to a formula. The fuel bounds
the recursion depth; `linearMuDecode` supplies fuel `c + 1`, which exceeds every
formula's depth (see `linearDepth_le_code`).

articles.title: Decoding inverts the linear μ-calculus encoding
articles.statement: Decoding inverts encoding.

articles.title: Token-list decoding inverts linear μ-calculus token encoding
articles.statement: Decoding inverts token encoding.

articles.title: Decoding a linear μ-calculus token list to a formula
articles.statement:

articles.title: Decoding linear μ-calculus codes
articles.statement: Decode a `linearMuCode` number back to the formula it encodes.

articles.title: Formulas of the linear-time μ-calculus
articles.statement:
Formulas of the linear-time μ-calculus over atoms `Atom`, with de Bruijn
variables for the fixed-point binders.

articles.title: Fuelled parsing inverts linear μ-calculus token encoding
articles.statement: Parsing inverts token encoding, with enough fuel.

articles.title: Fuelled parser for linear μ-calculus token lists
articles.statement:
Fuelled parsing of a `linearMuTokens` token list back to a formula,
returning the formula and the unconsumed suffix. The fuel bounds the
recursion depth; `linearMuDecodeList` supplies fuel `l.length + 1`, which
exceeds the token length of every formula encoded in `l`.

articles.title: Token-list encoding of linear μ-calculus formulas
articles.statement:
A polynomial-size token-list encoding of linear μ-calculus formulas over
`ℕ` atoms, used for the complexity statements in `WantedExt`. Each connective
contributes one tag token (`Nat.pair` of a small tag with `0`), and each atom
or variable contributes one token `Nat.pair tag value`, whose binary size is
`O(log value)`. The canonical bitstring encoding of a `List ℕ` delimits each
token, so the bitstring for a formula has length linear in the number of
connectives plus the total binary size of its atoms: `next^d (atom 0)` is
encoded by exactly `d + 1` tokens, unlike its Cantor-paired `linearMuCode`,
whose binary length is exponential in `d`.

articles.title: Park induction
articles.statement:

articles.title: Satisfaction of linear μ-calculus formulas
articles.statement:
Satisfaction of a linear μ-calculus formula at a position of the word
`val`. `μ X. φ` is the least pre-fixed point of `S ↦ ⟦φ⟧[X ↦ S]`, stated
directly as an infimum over pre-fixed points; `ν X. φ` is the greatest
post-fixed point, stated as a supremum over post-fixed points.

articles.title: The CTL model checker as a Boolean decision procedure
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a labelled
transition system with finitely many states and finitely many labels, decidable transitions and
decidable equality of states, and let $V$ be a decidable valuation of atoms at states. For a state
$s$ and a CTL formula $\varphi$, the model checker returns true exactly when $s$ belongs to the
set of states that the satisfaction-set algorithm computes for $\varphi$ in $\mathcal{T}$ under
$V$.

articles.title: Finite existential-globally set
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a labelled transition system with
finitely many states and finitely many labels, decidable transitions and decidable equality of
states, and let $A$ be a set of states. For a set $Z$ of states write
$\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ for the set of states having a transition into $Z$. The
existential-globally set of $A$ is obtained by applying the map
$Z \mapsto A \cap \mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ to the set of all states $n$ times, where $n$ is the
number of states.

Since this map is monotone, the iteration has stabilized after $n$ steps and the result is its
greatest fixed point.

articles.title: Finite existential-until set
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a labelled transition system with
finitely many states and finitely many labels, decidable transitions and decidable equality of
states, and let $A$ and $B$ be sets of states. For a set $Z$ of states write
$\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ for the set of states having a transition into $Z$. The
existential-until set with side set $A$ and target set $B$ is obtained by applying the map
$Z \mapsto B \cup (A \cap \mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z))$ to the empty set $n$ times, where $n$ is the
number of states.

Since this map is monotone, the iteration has stabilized after $n$ steps and the result is its
least fixed point.

articles.title: Every state starts a maximal path
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system, for every state $s$
there is an infinite run $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ with $s_0 = s$, or there are a sequence of states
$s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ with $s_0 = s$ and a $k$ such that $s_0, \dots, s_k$ is a finite run of
length $k$ and $s_k$ is deadlocked, that is, has no outgoing transition.

The proof iterates a chosen successor function and uses the axiom of choice.

articles.title: Existential next via the predecessor operator
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a
valuation of atoms, let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula and write $\mathrm{Sat}(\varphi)$ for the set
of states satisfying $\varphi$. A state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EX}\,\varphi$ if and only if $s$
belongs to the existential predecessor set of $\mathrm{Sat}(\varphi)$, that is, some transition
leads from $s$ to a state satisfying $\varphi$.

articles.title: Congruence of existential until in its target
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a
valuation of atoms, let $\rho$, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be CTL formulas such that every state
satisfies $\alpha$ if and only if it satisfies $\beta$. Then every state $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{E}[\rho \,\mathsf{U}\, \alpha]$ if and only if it satisfies
$\mathsf{E}[\rho \,\mathsf{U}\, \beta]$.

articles.title: Existential until as a least fixed point
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a
valuation of atoms, let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL formulas, write $\mathrm{Sat}(\chi)$ for the
set of states satisfying a formula $\chi$, and write $\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ for the set of
states having a transition into a set $Z$ of states. Then the set of states satisfying
$\mathsf{E}[\varphi \,\mathsf{U}\, \psi]$ is the least fixed point of the monotone map
$Z \mapsto \mathrm{Sat}(\psi) \cup (\mathrm{Sat}(\varphi) \cap \mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z))$ on sets
of states.

One inclusion is Park induction via the one-step expansion of
$\mathsf{E}[\varphi \,\mathsf{U}\, \psi]$; the other is induction on the length of the
witnessing finite run, unfolding the fixed point once per step.

articles.title: The existential-until functional
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a valuation of
atoms, let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL formulas. The existential-until functional sends a set $Z$
of states to the set of states $s$ such that either $s$ satisfies $\psi$, or $s$ satisfies
$\varphi$ and some transition leads from $s$ to a state in $Z$.

Its least fixed point is the set of states satisfying $\mathsf{E}[\varphi \,\mathsf{U}\, \psi]$.

articles.title: The existential-until functional as a monotone map
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with
a valuation of atoms, let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL formulas. The map sending a set $Z$ of
states to the set of states $s$ such that either $s$ satisfies $\psi$, or $s$ satisfies $\varphi$
and some transition leads from $s$ to a state in $Z$, is monotone for inclusion; this is that
map, regarded as an order-preserving map on sets of states.

articles.title: Deadlock-correct duality for AF
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a valuation of
atoms, let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. A state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{AF}\,\varphi$ if and only
if $s$ satisfies neither $\mathsf{E}[\neg\varphi \,\mathsf{U}\, (\neg\varphi \wedge
\neg\mathsf{EX}\,\top)]$ nor $\mathsf{EG}\,\neg\varphi$.

This is the case $\mathsf{A}[\top \,\mathsf{U}\, \varphi]$ of the duality for universal until.
The formula $\neg\mathsf{EX}\,\top$ holds exactly at deadlocked states, so the first disjunct
catches finite maximal paths that end at a deadlock without reaching $\varphi$.

articles.title: Bad target of the deadlock-correct until duality
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL
formulas, and write $t \models \chi$ when the state $t$ of a labelled transition system satisfies
the formula $\chi$ under a given valuation of the atoms. Then
$t \models \neg\psi \land (\neg\varphi \lor \neg\mathsf{EX}\,\top)$ if and only if
$t \not\models \psi$ and either $t \not\models \varphi$ or $t$ is deadlocked, that is, there is no
label $a$ and state $u$ with a transition from $t$ to $u$ labelled $a$.

articles.title: One-step unfolding of universal until, forward direction
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL
formulas, and write $s \models \chi$ when the state $s$ of a labelled transition system satisfies
the formula $\chi$ under a given valuation of the atoms. If
$s \models \mathsf{A}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi]$, then either $s \models \psi$, or
$s \models \varphi$, $s$ has at least one outgoing transition, and every state $t$ reached from $s$
by a single transition with any label satisfies
$t \models \mathsf{A}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi]$.

articles.title: Deadlock-correct duality for universal until
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL formulas,
and write $s \models \chi$ when the state $s$ of a labelled transition system satisfies the
formula $\chi$ under a given valuation of the atoms. Then
$s \models \mathsf{A}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi]$ if and only if neither
$s \models \mathsf{E}[\neg\psi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} (\neg\psi \land (\neg\varphi \lor
\neg\mathsf{EX}\,\top))]$ nor $s \models \mathsf{EG}\,\neg\psi$.

Here $\neg\mathsf{EX}\,\top$ holds exactly at the deadlocked states, those with no outgoing
transition. So $\mathsf{A}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi]$ fails at $s$ exactly when some
infinite run starting at $s$ stays in $\neg\psi$ forever, or some finite run starting at $s$ stays
in $\neg\psi$ up to a $\neg\psi$-state at which $\varphi$ fails or which is deadlocked.

articles.title: Correctness of the finite fixed-point computation of EG
articles.statement:
Let a labelled transition system
have finitely many states and finitely many labels, with decidable transitions and decidable
equality of states, and fix a valuation of the atoms. For a finite set $Z$ of states let
$\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ be the set of states with a transition into $Z$, and for a finite set
$A$ of states let $\mathrm{EG}_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ be the greatest fixed point of
$Z \mapsto A \cap \mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$, computed by finite iteration. Let $\varphi$ be a CTL
formula and $A$ a finite set of states such that a state lies in $A$ exactly when it satisfies
$\varphi$. Then every state $s$ lies in $\mathrm{EG}_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ if and only if $s$
satisfies $\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$.

articles.title: Correctness of the finite fixed-point computation of EU
articles.statement:
Let a labelled transition system
have finitely many states and finitely many labels, with decidable transitions and decidable
equality of states, and fix a valuation of the atoms. For a finite set $Z$ of states let
$\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ be the set of states with a transition into $Z$, and for finite sets
$A$ and $B$ of states let $\mathrm{EU}_{\mathrm{fin}}(A, B)$ be the least fixed point of
$Z \mapsto B \cup (A \cap \mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z))$, computed by finite iteration. Let $\varphi$
and $\psi$ be CTL formulas and $A$ and $B$ finite sets of states such that a state lies in $A$
exactly when it satisfies $\varphi$, and lies in $B$ exactly when it satisfies $\psi$. Then every
state $s$ lies in $\mathrm{EU}_{\mathrm{fin}}(A, B)$ if and only if $s$ satisfies
$\mathsf{E}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi]$.

articles.title: Correctness of the CTL model checker
articles.statement:
Let a labelled transition system have finitely many
states and finitely many labels, with decidable transitions and decidable equality of states, and
let the valuation of the atoms be decidable. For every CTL formula $\varphi$ and every state $s$,
the state $s$ lies in the set $\mathrm{sat}(\varphi)$ computed by the model checker if and only if
$s$ satisfies $\varphi$.

The proof is by induction on $\varphi$. The temporal cases use the correctness of the finite
fixed-point computations of $\mathsf{EU}$ and $\mathsf{EG}$, and the $\mathsf{AU}$ case also
identifies the computed bad-target set with the states satisfying the bad-target formula.

articles.title: Deadlocked states are exactly those satisfying ¬EX ⊤
articles.statement:
A state $s$ of a labelled transition
system satisfies the CTL formula $\neg\mathsf{EX}\,\top$, under any valuation of the atoms, if and
only if $s$ is deadlocked: there is no label $a$ and state $t$ with a transition from $s$ to $t$
labelled $a$.

articles.title: Finite existential predecessor set
articles.statement:
Let a labelled transition system have finitely many
states and finitely many labels, with decidable transitions. For a finite set $Z$ of states, its
existential predecessor set is the finite set of states $s$ for which there are a label $a$ and a
state $t \in Z$ with a transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled $a$.

It agrees with the existential predecessor operator applied to membership in $Z$.

articles.title: Finite-state CTL model checking by structural recursion
articles.statement:
The set of states satisfying a CTL formula in a finite system,
computed by structural recursion: atoms by filtering the valuation,
`EX` by `preExistsFin`, `EU` and `EG` by the finite fixed points
`eUntilFin` and `eGloballyFin`, and `AU` by complementing the
deadlock-correct duality of `Satisfies.forallUntil_iff_not` (the
bad-target set is built from the complement sets of the subformulas
and `preExistsFin lts Finset.univ`, the set of non-deadlocked
states).
